title: 老人與海
author: Ernest Hemingway 歐內斯特·海明威
description: 《The Old Man and the Sea》(1952)。古巴老漁夫聖地亞哥連續八十四天一無所獲,第八十五天獨自駛向灣流深處,與一條巨大的馬林魚搏鬥三天三夜,最後把魚拖回,卻在歸途中被鯊魚啃光。「人可以被毀滅,但不能被打敗」。海明威憑此獲1953年普立茲獎及1954年諾貝爾文學獎。英文原文對照廣東話/普通話翻譯。

chapters.title: I. The Old Man and the Boy 老人與男孩

passages.original: He was an old man who fished alone in a skiff in the Gulf Stream and he had gone eighty-four days now without taking a fish. In the first forty days a boy had been with him. But after forty days without a fish the boy’s parents had told him that the old man was now definitely and finally salao, which is the worst form of unlucky, and the boy had gone at their orders in another boat which caught three good fish the first week. It made the boy sad to see the old man come in each day with his skiff empty and he always went down to help him carry either the coiled lines or the gaff and harpoon and the sail that was furled around the mast. The sail was patched with flour sacks and, furled, it looked like the flag of permanent defeat.
passages.vernacular: 佢係一個老人,獨自駕住一條小艇喺灣流中捕魚,至今已經八十四天冇捕到一條魚喇。頭四十天裡,有一個男孩同佢喺一起。但四十天冇魚之後,男孩嘅父母告訴佢,老人而家肯定而且徹底係「薩勞」喇,嗰個係最壞嘅一種倒楣,於是男孩奉命上咗另一條船,嗰條船頭一個星期就捕到咗三條好魚。睇到老人每天空住小艇回嚟,男孩好難過,佢總是下去幫佢攞盤好嘅釣索,或係魚叉同魚鉤,仲有捲喺桅杆上嘅帆。嗰張帆用麵粉袋補過,捲起嚟時,睇上去像係永久失敗嘅旗幟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是一個老人,獨自駕著一條小艇在灣流中捕魚,至今已經八十四天沒有捕到一條魚了。頭四十天裡,有一個男孩同他在一起。但四十天沒有魚之後,男孩的父母告訴他,老人現在肯定而且徹底是「薩勞」了,那是最壞的一種倒楣,於是男孩奉命上了另一條船,那條船頭一個星期就捕到了三條好魚。看到老人每天空著小艇回來,男孩很難過,他總是下去幫他拿盤好的釣索,或是魚叉和魚鉤,還有捲在桅杆上的帆。那張帆用麵粉袋補過,捲起來時,看上去像是永久失敗的旗幟。

passages.original: The old man was thin and gaunt with deep wrinkles in the back of his neck. The brown blotches of the benevolent skin cancer the sun brings from its reflection on the tropic sea were on his cheeks. The blotches ran well down the sides of his face and his hands had the deep-creased scars from handling heavy fish on the cords. But none of these scars were fresh. They were as old as erosions in a fishless desert.
passages.vernacular: 老人又瘦又憔悴,後頸上有深深嘅皺紋。熱帶海面反射陽光帶嚟嘅嗰種良性皮膚癌嘅褐色斑塊,長喺佢嘅臉頰上。斑塊一直蔓延到佢臉嘅兩側,佢嘅雙手因用繩索拉大魚而留下咗深深嘅疤痕。但呢啲疤痕冇一道係新嘅。佢哋像無魚沙漠中嘅侵蝕痕跡一樣古老。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老人又瘦又憔悴,後頸上有深深的皺紋。熱帶海面反射陽光帶來的那種良性皮膚癌的褐色斑塊,長在他的臉頰上。斑塊一直蔓延到他臉的兩側,他的雙手因用繩索拉大魚而留下了深深的疤痕。但這些疤痕沒有一道是新的。它們像無魚沙漠中的侵蝕痕跡一樣古老。

passages.original: Everything about him was old except his eyes and they were the same color as the sea and were cheerful and undefeated.
passages.vernacular: 佢身上嘅一切都係老嘅,除咗佢嘅眼睛,佢哋同海一樣嘅顏色,愉快而不曾被打敗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他身上的一切都是老的,除了他的眼睛,它們和海一樣的顏色,愉快而不曾被打敗。

passages.original: “Santiago,” the boy said to him as they climbed the bank from where the skiff was hauled up. “I could go with you again. We’ve made some money.”
passages.vernacular: 「聖地亞哥,」男孩對佢講,佢哋從小艇被拖上嚟嘅地方爬上河岸。「我可以再同你出海。我哋賺咗啲錢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聖地亞哥,」男孩對他說,他們從小艇被拖上來的地方爬上河岸。「我可以再同你出海。我們賺了一些錢。」

passages.original: The old man had taught the boy to fish and the boy loved him.
passages.vernacular: 老人教過男孩捕魚,男孩愛佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老人教過男孩捕魚,男孩愛他。

passages.original: “No,” the old man said. “You’re with a lucky boat. Stay with them.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,」老人講。「你喺一條走運嘅船上。留喺佢哋嗰度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,」老人說。「你在一條走運的船上。留在他們那裡。」

passages.original: “But remember how you went eighty-seven days without fish and then we caught big ones every day for three weeks.”
passages.vernacular: 「但係記得你有八十七天冇魚,然後我哋連續三個星期每天都捕到大魚。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是記得你有八十七天沒有魚,然後我們連續三個星期每天都捕到大魚。」

passages.original: “I remember,” the old man said. “I know you did not leave me because you doubted.”
passages.vernacular: 「我記得,」老人講。「我知道你離開我唔係因為懷疑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我記得,」老人說。「我知道你離開我不是因為懷疑。」

passages.original: “It was papa made me leave. I am a boy and I must obey him.”
passages.vernacular: 「係爸爸讓我離開嘅。我係個細路,我必須聽佢嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是爸爸讓我離開的。我是個孩子,我必須聽他的。」

passages.original: “I know,” the old man said. “It is quite normal.”
passages.vernacular: 「我知道,」老人講。「呢個好正常。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道,」老人說。「這很正常。」

passages.original: “He hasn’t much faith.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢冇多少信心。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他沒有多少信心。」

passages.original: “No,” the old man said. “But we have. Haven’t we?”
passages.vernacular: 「冇,」老人講。「但我哋有。係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,」老人說。「但我們有。是不是?」

passages.original: “Yes,” the boy said. “Can I offer you a beer on the Terrace and then we’ll take the stuff home.”
passages.vernacular: 「係,」男孩講。「我請你喺露台餐館飲杯啤酒,然後我哋把嘢攞回家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,」男孩說。「我請你在露台餐館喝杯啤酒,然後我們把東西拿回家。」

passages.original: “Why not?” the old man said. “Between fishermen.”
passages.vernacular: 「點解不呢?」老人講。「漁夫之間嘛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼不呢?」老人說。「漁夫之間嘛。」

passages.original: They sat on the Terrace and many of the fishermen made fun of the old man and he was not angry. Others, of the older fishermen, looked at him and were sad. But they did not show it and they spoke politely about the current and the depths they had drifted their lines at and the steady good weather and of what they had seen. The successful fishermen of that day were already in and had butchered their marlin out and carried them laid full length across two planks, with two men staggering at the end of each plank, to the fish house where they waited for the ice truck to carry them to the market in Havana. Those who had caught sharks had taken them to the shark factory on the other side of the cove where they were hoisted on a block and tackle, their livers removed, their fins cut off and their hides skinned out and their flesh cut into strips for salting.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋坐喺露台餐館,許多漁夫取笑老人,佢冇生氣。另啲,年紀較大嘅漁夫,睇住佢,感到難過。但佢哋冇表露出嚟,而係客氣地談論洋流,同佢哋放線嘅深度,穩定嘅好天氣,以及佢哋所見到嘅事。嗰天捕魚成功嘅漁夫已經進港,把佢哋嘅馬林魚剖好,放喺兩塊木板上整條抬住,每塊木板嘅末端各有兩個人搖搖晃晃地抬,運到魚屋,喺嗰度等冰車把佢哋運往哈瓦嗰嘅市場。嗰啲捕到鯊魚嘅人把牠哋送到海灣另一邊嘅鯊魚工廠,喺嗰度用滑輪組把牠哋吊起,取出肝臟,割掉鰭,剝下皮,把肉切成條用鹽醃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們坐在露台餐館,許多漁夫取笑老人,他沒有生氣。另一些,年紀較大的漁夫,看著他,感到難過。但他們沒有表露出來,而是客氣地談論洋流,和他們放線的深度,穩定的好天氣,以及他們所見到的事。那天捕魚成功的漁夫已經進港,把他們的馬林魚剖好,放在兩塊木板上整條抬著,每塊木板的末端各有兩個人搖搖晃晃地抬,運到魚屋,在那裡等冰車把它們運往哈瓦那的市場。那些捕到鯊魚的人把牠們送到海灣另一邊的鯊魚工廠,在那裡用滑輪組把牠們吊起,取出肝臟,割掉鰭,剝下皮,把肉切成條用鹽醃。

passages.original: When the wind was in the east a smell came across the harbour from the shark factory; but today there was only the faint edge of the odour because the wind had backed into the north and then dropped off and it was pleasant and sunny on the Terrace.
passages.vernacular: 風從東邊吹嚟時,有一股氣味從鯊魚工廠飄過港口;但今日只有淡淡嘅啲氣味,因為風向已轉向北方,然後平息喇,露台上天氣宜人,陽光燦爛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 風從東邊吹來時,有一股氣味從鯊魚工廠飄過港口;但今天只有淡淡的一點氣味,因為風向已轉向北方,然後平息了,露台上天氣宜人,陽光燦爛。

passages.original: “Santiago,” the boy said.
passages.vernacular: 「聖地亞哥,」男孩講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聖地亞哥,」男孩說。

passages.original: “Yes,” the old man said. He was holding his glass and thinking of many years ago.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」老人講。佢攞住杯子,想住許多年前嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」老人說。他拿著杯子,想著許多年前的事。

passages.original: “Can I go out to get sardines for you for tomorrow?”
passages.vernacular: 「我聽日可以出去幫你弄沙丁魚嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我明天可以出去幫你弄沙丁魚嗎?」

passages.original: “No. Go and play baseball. I can still row and Rogelio will throw the net.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔使。去打棒球吧。我仲能划船,羅赫略會撒網。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不用。去打棒球吧。我還能划船,羅赫略會撒網。」

passages.original: “I would like to go. If I cannot fish with you, I would like to serve in some way.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想去。如果我唔能夠同你一起捕魚,我想以某種方式為你效勞。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想去。如果我不能同你一起捕魚,我想以某種方式為你效勞。」

passages.original: “You bought me a beer,” the old man said. “You are already a man.”
passages.vernacular: 「你請我飲啤酒喇,」老人講。「你已經係個男子漢喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你請我喝啤酒了,」老人說。「你已經是個男子漢了。」

passages.original: “How old was I when you first took me in a boat?”
passages.vernacular: 「你第一次帶我上船時,我多大?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你第一次帶我上船時,我多大?」

passages.original: “Five and you nearly were killed when I brought the fish in too green and he nearly tore the boat to pieces. Can you remember?”
passages.vernacular: 「五歲,你差點被殺,嗰個係我把魚拖上嚟得太生,牠幾乎把船撕成碎片。你記得嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「五歲,你差點被殺,那是我把魚拖上來得太生,牠幾乎把船撕成碎片。你記得嗎?」

passages.original: “I can remember the tail slapping and banging and the thwart breaking and the noise of the clubbing. I can remember you throwing me into the bow where the wet coiled lines were and feeling the whole boat shiver and the noise of you clubbing him like chopping a tree down and the sweet blood smell all over me.”
passages.vernacular: 「我記得尾巴拍打撞擊,橫板斷裂,同棍棒敲打嘅聲音。我記得你把我扔到船頭,嗰度有濕嘅盤繩,感覺整條船都喺顫抖,同你像砍樹一樣用棍子打牠嘅聲音,仲有滿身嘅甜甜嘅血腥味。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我記得尾巴拍打撞擊,橫板斷裂,和棍棒敲打的聲音。我記得你把我扔到船頭,那裡有濕的盤繩,感覺整條船都在顫抖,和你像砍樹一樣用棍子打牠的聲音,還有滿身的甜甜的血腥味。」

passages.original: “Can you really remember that or did I just tell it to you?”
passages.vernacular: 「你真嘅記得,定係我只係告訴過你?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你真的記得,還是我只是告訴過你?」

passages.original: “I remember everything from when we first went together.”
passages.vernacular: 「我記得我哋第一次一起出海以來嘅一切。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我記得我們第一次一起出海以來的一切。」

passages.original: The old man looked at him with his sun-burned, confident loving eyes.
passages.vernacular: 老人用佢被太陽曬黑嘅、自信而充滿愛嘅眼睛睇住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老人用他被太陽曬黑的、自信而充滿愛的眼睛看著他。

passages.original: “If you were my boy I’d take you out and gamble,” he said. “But you are your father’s and your mother’s and you are in a lucky boat.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你係我嘅細路,我會帶你出去冒險,」佢講。「但你係你父母嘅,而且你喺一條走運嘅船上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你是我的孩子,我會帶你出去冒險,」他說。「但你是你父母的,而且你在一條走運的船上。」

passages.original: “May I get the sardines? I know where I can get four baits too.”
passages.vernacular: 「我可以去弄沙丁魚嗎?我都知道邊度可以弄到四條餌。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我可以去弄沙丁魚嗎?我也知道哪裡可以弄到四條餌。」

passages.original: “I have mine left from today. I put them in salt in the box.”
passages.vernacular: 「我今日剩下咗啲。我用鹽醃喺箱子裡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我今天剩下了一些。我用鹽醃在箱子裡。」

passages.original: “Let me get four fresh ones.”
passages.vernacular: 「讓我去弄四條新鮮嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓我去弄四條新鮮的。」

passages.original: “One,” the old man said. His hope and his confidence had never gone. But now they were freshening as when the breeze rises.
passages.vernacular: 「一條,」老人講。佢嘅希望同信心從未消失。但而家佢哋正在清新起嚟,像微風升起一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一條,」老人說。他的希望和信心從未消失。但現在它們正在清新起來,像微風升起一樣。

passages.original: “Two,” the boy said.
passages.vernacular: 「兩條,」男孩講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「兩條,」男孩說。

passages.original: “Two,” the old man agreed. “You didn’t steal them?”
passages.vernacular: 「兩條,」老人同意。「你唔係偷嘅吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「兩條,」老人同意。「你不是偷的吧?」

passages.original: “I would,” the boy said. “But I bought these.”
passages.vernacular: 「我會,」男孩講。「但呢啲係我買嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會,」男孩說。「但這些是我買的。」

passages.original: “Thank you,” the old man said. He was too simple to wonder when he had attained humility. But he knew he had attained it and he knew it was not disgraceful and it carried no loss of true pride.
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你,」老人講。佢太單純,冇想過自己乜嘢時候學會咗謙卑。但佢知道佢已經學會喇,都知道呢並不可恥,都冇損害真正嘅自尊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你,」老人說。他太單純,沒想過自己什麼時候學會了謙卑。但他知道他已經學會了,也知道這並不可恥,也沒有損害真正的自尊。

passages.original: “Tomorrow is going to be a good day with this current,” he said.
passages.vernacular: 「有呢股洋流,聽日會係個好日子,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有這股洋流,明天會是個好日子,」他說。

passages.original: “Where are you going?” the boy asked.
passages.vernacular: 「你去邊度?」男孩問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你去哪裡?」男孩問。

passages.original: “Far out to come in when the wind shifts. I want to be out before it is light.”
passages.vernacular: 「遠遠地出去,等風向轉變時回嚟。我想喺天亮前就出去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「遠遠地出去,等風向轉變時回來。我想在天亮前就出去。」

passages.original: “I’ll try to get him to work far out,” the boy said. “Then if you hook something truly big we can come to your aid.”
passages.vernacular: 「我會設法讓佢喺遠處工作,」男孩講。「咁如果你釣到真正大嘅,我哋可以來幫你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會設法讓他在遠處工作,」男孩說。「那麼如果你釣到真正大的,我們可以來幫你。」

passages.original: “He does not like to work too far out.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢不鍾意喺太遠嘅地方工作。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他不喜歡在太遠的地方工作。」

passages.original: “No,” the boy said. “But I will see something that he cannot see such as a bird working and get him to come out after dolphin.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,」男孩講。「但我會睇見佢睇唔到嘅嘢,比如有鳥喺忙,設法讓佢出嚟追鬼頭刀。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,」男孩說。「但我會看見他看不到的東西,比如有鳥在忙,設法讓他出來追鬼頭刀。」

passages.original: “Are his eyes that bad?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢嘅眼睛咁壞嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他的眼睛那麼壞嗎?」

passages.original: “He is almost blind.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢幾乎瞎喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他幾乎瞎了。」

passages.original: “It is strange,” the old man said. “He never went turtle-ing. That is what kills the eyes.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個好奇怪,」老人講。「佢從冇去獵過海龜。嗰才係傷眼睛嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這很奇怪,」老人說。「他從沒去獵過海龜。那才是傷眼睛的。」

passages.original: “But you went turtle-ing for years off the Mosquito Coast and your eyes are good.”
passages.vernacular: 「但你多年喺蚊子海岸外獵海龜,你嘅眼睛好好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但你多年在蚊子海岸外獵海龜,你的眼睛很好。」

passages.original: “I am a strange old man.”
passages.vernacular: 「我係個奇怪嘅老頭。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是個奇怪的老頭。」

passages.original: “But are you strong enough now for a truly big fish?”
passages.vernacular: 「但你而家強壯到能對付真正嘅大魚嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但你現在強壯到能對付真正的大魚嗎?」

passages.original: “I think so. And there are many tricks.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想可以。而且有許多竅門。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想可以。而且有許多竅門。」

passages.original: “Let us take the stuff home,” the boy said. “So I can get the cast net and go after the sardines.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋把嘢攞回家吧,」男孩講。「咁樣我可以攞撒網,去弄沙丁魚。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們把東西拿回家吧,」男孩說。「這樣我可以拿撒網,去弄沙丁魚。」

passages.original: They picked up the gear from the boat. The old man carried the mast on his shoulder and the boy carried the wooden box with the coiled, hard-braided brown lines, the gaff and the harpoon with its shaft. The box with the baits was under the stern of the skiff along with the club that was used to subdue the big fish when they were brought alongside. No one would steal from the old man but it was better to take the sail and the heavy lines home as the dew was bad for them and, though he was quite sure no local people would steal from him, the old man thought that a gaff and a harpoon were needless temptations to leave in a boat.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋從船上攞起裝備。老人把桅杆扛喺肩上,男孩提住木箱,裡面係盤好嘅、緊緊編織嘅棕色釣索、魚鉤同帶桿嘅魚叉。裝餌嘅箱子連同用嚟制服靠近船邊嘅大魚嘅棍子,放喺小艇嘅船尾下面。冇人會偷老人嘅嘢,但最好把帆同粗釣索帶回家,因為露水對佢哋不好,雖然佢好肯定本地人唔會偷佢嘅嘢,老人認為把魚鉤同魚叉留喺船上係唔使要嘅誘惑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們從船上拿起裝備。老人把桅杆扛在肩上,男孩提著木箱,裡面是盤好的、緊緊編織的棕色釣索、魚鉤和帶桿的魚叉。裝餌的箱子連同用來制服靠近船邊的大魚的棍子,放在小艇的船尾下面。沒有人會偷老人的東西,但最好把帆和粗釣索帶回家,因為露水對它們不好,雖然他很肯定本地人不會偷他的東西,老人認為把魚鉤和魚叉留在船上是不必要的誘惑。

passages.original: They walked up the road together to the old man’s shack and went in through its open door. The old man leaned the mast with its wrapped sail against the wall and the boy put the box and the other gear beside it. The mast was nearly as long as the one room of the shack. The shack was made of the tough bud-shields of the royal palm which are called guano and in it there was a bed, a table, one chair, and a place on the dirt floor to cook with charcoal. On the brown walls of the flattened, overlapping leaves of the sturdy fibered guano there was a picture in color of the Sacred Heart of Jesus and another of the Virgin of Cobre. These were relics of his wife. Once there had been a tinted photograph of his wife on the wall but he had taken it down because it made him too lonely to see it and it was on the shelf in the corner under his clean shirt.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋沿住路一起走到老人嘅小屋,從敞開嘅門走進去。老人把裹住帆嘅桅杆靠喺牆上,男孩把箱子同其他裝備放喺佢旁邊。桅杆幾乎同小屋唯一嘅房間一樣長。小屋係用王棕堅韌嘅葉鞘做成嘅,叫做瓜諾,裡面有一張床、一張桌子、一把椅子,同泥地上用木炭做飯嘅地方。喺用堅韌纖維嘅瓜諾壓扁、重疊嘅葉子做嘅褐色牆壁上,有一幅彩色嘅耶穌聖心像,同另一幅科夫雷聖母像。呢啲都係佢妻子嘅遺物。牆上曾經有一張佢妻子嘅住色照片,但佢把佢取下嚟喇,因為睇到佢使佢太孤獨,佢放喺角落嘅架子上,佢乾淨嘅襯衫下面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們沿著路一起走到老人的小屋,從敞開的門走進去。老人把裹著帆的桅杆靠在牆上,男孩把箱子和其他裝備放在它旁邊。桅杆幾乎和小屋唯一的房間一樣長。小屋是用王棕堅韌的葉鞘做成的,叫做瓜諾,裡面有一張床、一張桌子、一把椅子,和泥地上用木炭做飯的地方。在用堅韌纖維的瓜諾壓扁、重疊的葉子做的褐色牆壁上,有一幅彩色的耶穌聖心像,和另一幅科夫雷聖母像。這些都是他妻子的遺物。牆上曾經有一張他妻子的著色照片,但他把它取下來了,因為看到它使他太孤獨,它放在角落的架子上,他乾淨的襯衫下面。

passages.original: “What do you have to eat?” the boy asked.
passages.vernacular: 「你有乜嘢食嘅?」男孩問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你有什麼吃的?」男孩問。

passages.original: “A pot of yellow rice with fish. Do you want some?”
passages.vernacular: 「一鍋魚黃飯。你要食啲嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一鍋魚黃飯。你要吃一些嗎?」

passages.original: “No. I will eat at home. Do you want me to make the fire?”
passages.vernacular: 「不。我回家食。你要我生火嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不。我回家吃。你要我生火嗎?」

passages.original: “No. I will make it later on. Or I may eat the rice cold.”
passages.vernacular: 「不。我待會兒再生。或者我可以食冷飯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不。我待會兒再生。或者我可以吃冷飯。」

passages.original: “May I take the cast net?”
passages.vernacular: 「我可以攞撒網嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我可以拿撒網嗎?」

passages.original: “Of course.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然。」

passages.original: There was no cast net and the boy remembered when they had sold it. But they went through this fiction every day. There was no pot of yellow rice and fish and the boy knew this too.
passages.vernacular: 冇撒網,男孩記得佢哋係乜嘢時候賣掉嘅。但佢哋每天都經歷咁樣嘅虛構。冇一鍋魚黃飯,男孩都知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有撒網,男孩記得它們是什麼時候賣掉的。但他們每天都經歷這樣的虛構。沒有一鍋魚黃飯,男孩也知道。

passages.original: “Eighty-five is a lucky number,” the old man said. “How would you like to see me bring one in that dressed out over a thousand pounds?”
passages.vernacular: 「八十五係個幸運數字,」老人講。「你想睇我拖一條開膛後超過一千磅嘅回嚟嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「八十五是個幸運數字,」老人說。「你想看我拖一條開膛後超過一千磅的回來嗎?」

passages.original: “I’ll get the cast net and go for sardines. Will you sit in the sun in the doorway?”
passages.vernacular: 「我去攞撒網,去弄沙丁魚。你坐喺門口曬太陽好嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我去拿撒網,去弄沙丁魚。你坐在門口曬太陽好嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes. I have yesterday’s paper and I will read the baseball.”
passages.vernacular: 「好。我有尋日嘅報紙,我睇棒球。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好。我有昨天的報紙,我看棒球。」

passages.original: The boy did not know whether yesterday’s paper was a fiction too. But the old man brought it out from under the bed.
passages.vernacular: 男孩唔知道尋日嘅報紙係唔係都係虛構嘅。但老人從床底下把佢攞出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩不知道昨天的報紙是不是也是虛構的。但老人從床底下把它拿出來。

passages.original: “Perico gave it to me at the bodega,” he explained.
passages.vernacular: 「佩里科喺雜貨店畀我嘅,」佢解釋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「佩里科在雜貨店給我的,」他解釋。

passages.original: “I’ll be back when I have the sardines. I’ll keep yours and mine together on ice and we can share them in the morning. When I come back you can tell me about the baseball.”
passages.vernacular: 「我弄到沙丁魚就回嚟。我會把你嘅同我嘅一起放喺冰上,朝早我哋可以分。我回嚟時你可以告訴我棒球嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我弄到沙丁魚就回來。我會把你的和我的一起放在冰上,早上我們可以分。我回來時你可以告訴我棒球的事。」

passages.original: “The Yankees cannot lose.”
passages.vernacular: 「洋基隊唔會輸。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「洋基隊不會輸。」

passages.original: “But I fear the Indians of Cleveland.”
passages.vernacular: 「但我怕克利夫蘭印第安人隊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我怕克利夫蘭印第安人隊。」

passages.original: “Have faith in the Yankees my son. Think of the great DiMaggio.”
passages.vernacular: 「對洋基隊有信心,我嘅細路。想想偉大嘅迪馬喬。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對洋基隊有信心,我的孩子。想想偉大的迪馬喬。」

passages.original: “I fear both the Tigers of Detroit and the Indians of Cleveland.”
passages.vernacular: 「我怕底特律老虎隊同克利夫蘭印第安人隊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我怕底特律老虎隊和克利夫蘭印第安人隊。」

passages.original: “Be careful or you will fear even the Reds of Cincinnati and the White Sox of Chicago.”
passages.vernacular: 「小心,否則你連辛辛嗰提紅人隊同芝加哥白襪隊都要怕喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「小心,否則你連辛辛那提紅人隊和芝加哥白襪隊都要怕了。」

passages.original: “You study it and tell me when I come back.”
passages.vernacular: 「你研究研究,我回嚟時告訴我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你研究研究,我回來時告訴我。」

passages.original: “Do you think we should buy a terminal of the lottery with an eighty-five? Tomorrow is the eighty-fifth day.”
passages.vernacular: 「你想我哋該買一張尾數係八十五嘅彩票嗎?聽日係第八十五天。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你想我們該買一張尾數是八十五的彩票嗎?明天是第八十五天。」

passages.original: “We can do that,” the boy said. “But what about the eighty-seven of your great record?”
passages.vernacular: 「可以,」男孩講。「但你嗰八十七嘅偉大紀錄呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可以,」男孩說。「但你那八十七的偉大紀錄呢?」

passages.original: “It could not happen twice. Do you think you can find an eighty-five?”
passages.vernacular: 「唔可能發生兩次。你想你能找到八十五嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不可能發生兩次。你想你能找到八十五嗎?」

passages.original: “I can order one.”
passages.vernacular: 「我可以訂一張。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我可以訂一張。」

passages.original: “One sheet. That’s two dollars and a half. Who can we borrow that from?”
passages.vernacular: 「一張。嗰個係兩塊半。我哋向邊個借?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一張。那是兩塊半。我們向誰借?」

passages.original: “That’s easy. I can always borrow two dollars and a half.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢容易。兩塊半我總能借到。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這容易。兩塊半我總能借到。」

passages.original: “I think perhaps I can too. But I try not to borrow. First you borrow. Then you beg.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想或者我都能。但我盡量不借。先係借。然後係乞討。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想也許我也能。但我盡量不借。先是借。然後是乞討。」

passages.original: “Keep warm old man,” the boy said. “Remember we are in September.”
passages.vernacular: 「保暖,老人家,」男孩講。「記住我哋而家係九月。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「保暖,老人家,」男孩說。「記住我們現在是九月。」

passages.original: “The month when the great fish come,” the old man said. “Anyone can be a fisherman in May.”
passages.vernacular: 「大魚嚟嘅月份,」老人講。「五月邊個都能做漁夫。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「大魚來的月份,」老人說。「五月誰都能做漁夫。」

passages.original: “I go now for the sardines,” the boy said.
passages.vernacular: 「我而家去弄沙丁魚,」男孩講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我現在去弄沙丁魚,」男孩說。

passages.original: When the boy came back the old man was asleep in the chair and the sun was down. The boy took the old army blanket off the bed and spread it over the back of the chair and over the old man’s shoulders. They were strange shoulders, still powerful although very old, and the neck was still strong too and the creases did not show so much when the old man was asleep and his head fallen forward. His shirt had been patched so many times that it was like the sail and the patches were faded to many different shades by the sun. The old man’s head was very old though and with his eyes closed there was no life in his face. The newspaper lay across his knees and the weight of his arm held it there in the evening breeze. He was barefooted.
passages.vernacular: 男孩回嚟時,老人坐喺椅子上瞓住喇,太陽已經下山。男孩把床上嘅舊軍毯攞下嚟,蓋喺椅背同老人嘅肩上。嗰個係奇特嘅肩膀,雖然好老,仍然強壯,脖子都仍然結實,老人瞓住、頭向前垂時,皺紋都不咁明顯。佢嘅襯衫補過咁多次,像嗰張帆一樣,補丁被太陽曬成許多種不同嘅色調。然而老人嘅頭好老喇,閉住眼睛,臉上冇生氣。報紙橫喺佢嘅膝上,佢手臂嘅重量喺晚風中壓住佢。佢光住腳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩回來時,老人坐在椅子上睡著了,太陽已經下山。男孩把床上的舊軍毯拿下來,蓋在椅背和老人的肩上。那是奇特的肩膀,雖然很老,仍然強壯,脖子也仍然結實,老人睡著、頭向前垂時,皺紋也不那麼明顯。他的襯衫補過那麼多次,像那張帆一樣,補丁被太陽曬成許多種不同的色調。然而老人的頭很老了,閉著眼睛,臉上沒有生氣。報紙橫在他的膝上,他手臂的重量在晚風中壓著它。他光著腳。

passages.original: The boy left him there and when he came back the old man was still asleep.
passages.vernacular: 男孩把佢留喺嗰度,佢回嚟時老人仲喺瞓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩把他留在那裡,他回來時老人還在睡。

passages.original: “Wake up old man,” the boy said and put his hand on one of the old man’s knees.
passages.vernacular: 「醒醒,老人家,」男孩講,把手放喺老人嘅一隻膝蓋上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「醒醒,老人家,」男孩說,把手放在老人的一隻膝蓋上。

passages.original: The old man opened his eyes and for a moment he was coming back from a long way away. Then he smiled.
passages.vernacular: 老人睜開眼睛,有一刻佢係從好遠嘅地方回嚟。然後佢笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老人睜開眼睛,有一刻他是從很遠的地方回來。然後他笑了。

passages.original: “What have you got?” he asked.
passages.vernacular: 「你攞咗乜嘢?」佢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你拿了什麼?」他問。

passages.original: “Supper,” said the boy. “We’re going to have supper.”
passages.vernacular: 「晚飯,」男孩講。「我哋嚟食晚飯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「晚飯,」男孩說。「我們來吃晚飯。」

passages.original: “I’m not very hungry.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不太餓。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不太餓。」

passages.original: “Come on and eat. You can’t fish and not eat.”
passages.vernacular: 「嚟食吧。你唔能夠捕魚而不食嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「來吃吧。你不能捕魚而不吃東西。」

passages.original: “I have,” the old man said getting up and taking the newspaper and folding it. Then he started to fold the blanket.
passages.vernacular: 「我食過喇,」老人講,站起嚟,攞起報紙折好。然後佢開始折毯子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我吃過了,」老人說,站起來,拿起報紙折好。然後他開始折毯子。

passages.original: “Keep the blanket around you,” the boy said. “You’ll not fish without eating while I’m alive.”
passages.vernacular: 「把毯子圍喺身上,」男孩講。「我活住一天,你就唔能夠不食嘢去捕魚。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「把毯子圍在身上,」男孩說。「我活著一天,你就不能不吃東西去捕魚。」

passages.original: “Then live a long time and take care of yourself,” the old man said. “What are we eating?”
passages.vernacular: 「咁活得長長久久,照顧好自己,」老人講。「我哋食乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼活得長長久久,照顧好自己,」老人說。「我們吃什麼?」

passages.original: “Black beans and rice, fried bananas, and some stew.”
passages.vernacular: 「黑豆飯、炸香蕉,同啲燉菜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「黑豆飯、炸香蕉,和一些燉菜。」

passages.original: The boy had brought them in a two-decker metal container from the Terrace. The two sets of knives and forks and spoons were in his pocket with a paper napkin wrapped around each set.
passages.vernacular: 男孩用一個兩層嘅金屬飯盒從露台餐館帶嚟。兩套刀叉同湯匙放喺佢口袋裡,每一套都包住一張紙餐巾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩用一個兩層的金屬飯盒從露台餐館帶來。兩套刀叉和湯匙放在他口袋裡,每一套都包著一張紙餐巾。

passages.original: “Who gave this to you?”
passages.vernacular: 「邊個畀你嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「誰給你的?」

passages.original: “Martin. The owner.”
passages.vernacular: 「馬丁。店主。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬丁。店主。」

passages.original: “I must thank him.”
passages.vernacular: 「我得謝謝佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我得謝謝他。」

passages.original: “I thanked him already,” the boy said. “You don’t need to thank him.”
passages.vernacular: 「我已經謝過佢喇,」男孩講。「你不需要謝佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我已經謝過他了,」男孩說。「你不需要謝他。」

passages.original: “I’ll give him the belly meat of a big fish,” the old man said. “Has he done this for us more than once?”
passages.vernacular: 「我畀佢一條大魚嘅肚腩肉,」老人講。「佢為我哋咁樣做不止一次咗吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我給他一條大魚的肚腩肉,」老人說。「他為我們這樣做不止一次了吧?」

passages.original: “I think so.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想係嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想是的。」

passages.original: “I must give him something more than the belly meat then. He is very thoughtful for us.”
passages.vernacular: 「咁我必須畀佢比肚腩肉更多嘅嘢。佢對我哋好體貼。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼我必須給他比肚腩肉更多的東西。他對我們非常體貼。」

passages.original: “He sent two beers.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢送咗兩瓶啤酒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他送了兩瓶啤酒。」

passages.original: “I like the beer in cans best.”
passages.vernacular: 「我最鍾意罐裝啤酒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我最喜歡罐裝啤酒。」

passages.original: “I know. But this is in bottles, Hatuey beer, and I take back the bottles.”
passages.vernacular: 「我知道。但呢個係瓶裝嘅,阿圖埃啤酒,我要把瓶子仲回去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道。但這是瓶裝的,阿圖埃啤酒,我要把瓶子還回去。」

passages.original: “That’s very kind of you,” the old man said. “Should we eat?”
passages.vernacular: 「你真好心,」老人講。「我哋食嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你真好心,」老人說。「我們吃嗎?」

passages.original: “I’ve been asking you to,” the boy told him gently. “I have not wished to open the container until you were ready.”
passages.vernacular: 「我一直喺請你食,」男孩溫和地對佢講。「我唔想喺你準備好之前打開飯盒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我一直在請你吃,」男孩溫和地對他說。「我不想在你準備好之前打開飯盒。」

passages.original: “I’m ready now,” the old man said. “I only needed time to wash.”
passages.vernacular: 「我而家準備好喇,」老人講。「我只需要時間洗一洗。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我現在準備好了,」老人說。「我只需要時間洗一洗。」

passages.original: Where did you wash? the boy thought. The village water supply was two streets down the road. I must have water here for him, the boy thought, and soap and a good towel. Why am I so thoughtless? I must get him another shirt and a jacket for the winter and some sort of shoes and another blanket.
passages.vernacular: 你喺邊度洗?男孩想。村裡嘅供水處喺街道盡頭兩條街外。我必須喺呢度為佢準備水,男孩想,仲有肥皂同一條好毛巾。我點解咁不體貼?我必須畀佢再弄一件襯衫同一件冬天穿嘅外套,同某種鞋子,仲有另一條毯子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在哪裡洗?男孩想。村裡的供水處在街道盡頭兩條街外。我必須在這裡為他準備水,男孩想,還有肥皂和一條好毛巾。我為什麼這麼不體貼?我必須給他再弄一件襯衫和一件冬天穿的外套,和某種鞋子,還有另一條毯子。

passages.original: “Your stew is excellent,” the old man said.
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅燉菜好棒,」老人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的燉菜很棒,」老人說。

passages.original: “Tell me about the baseball,” the boy asked him.
passages.vernacular: 「告訴我棒球嘅事,」男孩問佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「告訴我棒球的事,」男孩問他。

passages.original: “In the American League it is the Yankees as I said,” the old man said happily.
passages.vernacular: 「美國聯盟係洋基隊,正如我講嘅,」老人高興地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「美國聯盟是洋基隊,正如我說的,」老人高興地說。

passages.original: “They lost today,” the boy told him.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋今日輸喇,」男孩告訴佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們今天輸了,」男孩告訴他。

passages.original: “That means nothing. The great DiMaggio is himself again.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰冇乜嘢。偉大嘅迪馬喬又恢復咗本色。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那沒什麼。偉大的迪馬喬又恢復了本色。」

passages.original: “They have other men on the team.”
passages.vernacular: 「球隊仲有別嘅球員。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「球隊還有別的球員。」

passages.original: “Naturally. But he makes the difference. In the other league, between Brooklyn and Philadelphia I must take Brooklyn. But then I think of Dick Sisler and those great drives in the old park.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然。但佢起決定性作用。喺另一個聯盟,布魯克林同費城之間,我必須選布魯克林。但然後我想到迪克·西斯勒同老球場上嗰啲了不起嘅長打。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然。但他起決定性作用。在另一個聯盟,布魯克林和費城之間,我必須選布魯克林。但然後我想到迪克·西斯勒和老球場上那些了不起的長打。」

passages.original: “There was nothing ever like them. He hits the longest ball I have ever seen.”
passages.vernacular: 「從來冇像嗰樣嘅。佢打嘅球係我見過最遠嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從來沒有像那樣的。他打的球是我見過最遠的。」

passages.original: “Do you remember when he used to come to the Terrace? I wanted to take him fishing but I was too timid to ask him. Then I asked you to ask him and you were too timid.”
passages.vernacular: 「你記得佢以前常嚟露台餐館嗎?我想帶佢去捕魚,但我膽怯,唔敢請佢。然後我叫你去請佢,你都膽怯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你記得他以前常來露台餐館嗎?我想帶他去捕魚,但我膽怯,不敢請他。然後我叫你去請他,你也膽怯。」

passages.original: “I know. It was a great mistake. He might have gone with us. Then we would have that for all of our lives.”
passages.vernacular: 「我知道。嗰個係個大錯誤。佢本可以同我哋去嘅。嗰我哋呢輩子就都有嗰個喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道。那是個大錯誤。他本可以同我們去的。那我們這輩子就都有那個了。」

passages.original: “I would like to take the great DiMaggio fishing,” the old man said. “They say his father was a fisherman. Maybe he was as poor as we are and would understand.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想帶偉大嘅迪馬喬去捕魚,」老人講。「佢哋講佢父親係漁夫。或者佢同我哋一樣窮,會理解嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想帶偉大的迪馬喬去捕魚,」老人說。「他們說他父親是漁夫。也許他和我們一樣窮,會理解的。」

passages.original: “The great Sisler’s father was never poor and he, the father, was playing in the big leagues when he was my age.”
passages.vernacular: 「偉大嘅西斯勒嘅父親從來不窮,而且佢父親喺我呢個年紀時就喺大聯盟打球喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「偉大的西斯勒的父親從來不窮,而且他父親在我這個年紀時就在大聯盟打球了。」

passages.original: “When I was your age I was before the mast on a square rigged ship that ran to Africa and I have seen lions on the beaches in the evening.”
passages.vernacular: 「我喺你呢個年紀時,我喺一艘去非洲嘅橫帆船上當水手,傍晚我喺海灘上睇過獅子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我在你這個年紀時,我在一艘去非洲的橫帆船上當水手,傍晚我在海灘上看過獅子。」

passages.original: “I know. You told me.”
passages.vernacular: 「我知道。你告訴過我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道。你告訴過我。」

passages.original: “Should we talk about Africa or about baseball?”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋談非洲定係談棒球?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們談非洲還是談棒球?」

passages.original: “Baseball I think,” the boy said. “Tell me about the great John J. McGraw.” He said Jota for J.
passages.vernacular: 「棒球,我想,」男孩講。「告訴我偉大嘅約翰·J·麥格勞嘅事。」佢把J講成咗霍塔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「棒球,我想,」男孩說。「告訴我偉大的約翰·J·麥格勞的事。」他把J說成了霍塔。

passages.original: “He used to come to the Terrace sometimes too in the older days. But he was rough and harsh-spoken and difficult when he was drinking. His mind was on horses as well as baseball. At least he carried lists of horses at all times in his pocket and frequently spoke the names of horses on the telephone.”
passages.vernacular: 「以前佢有時都嚟露台餐館。但佢飲酒時粗魯、講話刻薄、難相處。佢嘅心思既喺賽即刻都喺棒球上。至少佢口袋裡隨時帶住馬嘅名單,並且常喺電話裡講出馬嘅名字。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「以前他有時也來露台餐館。但他喝酒時粗魯、說話刻薄、難相處。他的心思既在賽馬上也在棒球上。至少他口袋裡隨時帶著馬的名單,並且常在電話裡說出馬的名字。」

passages.original: “He was a great manager,” the boy said. “My father thinks he was the greatest.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢係個偉大嘅經理,」男孩講。「我父親認為佢係最偉大嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是個偉大的經理,」男孩說。「我父親認為他是最偉大的。」

passages.original: “Because he came here the most times,” the old man said. “If Durocher had continued to come here each year your father would think him the greatest manager.”
passages.vernacular: 「因為佢嚟呢度次數最多,」老人講。「如果杜羅切每年繼續嚟呢度,你父親會認為佢係最偉大嘅經理。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為他來這裡次數最多,」老人說。「如果杜羅切每年繼續來這裡,你父親會認為他是最偉大的經理。」

passages.original: “Who is the greatest manager, really, Luque or Mike Gonzalez?”
passages.vernacular: 「邊個係最偉大嘅經理,真嘅,盧克定係邁克·岡薩雷斯?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「誰是最偉大的經理,真的,盧克還是邁克·岡薩雷斯?」

passages.original: “I think they are equal.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想佢哋一樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想他們一樣。」

passages.original: “And the best fisherman is you.”
passages.vernacular: 「而最好嘅漁夫係你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而最好的漁夫是你。」

passages.original: “No. I know others better.”
passages.vernacular: 「不。我知道別人更好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不。我知道別人更好。」

passages.original: “Qu� va,” the boy said. “There are many good fishermen and some great ones. But there is only you.”
passages.vernacular: 「邊有嘅事,」男孩講。「有許多好漁夫,都有啲偉大嘅。但只有你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哪有的事,」男孩說。「有許多好漁夫,也有一些偉大的。但只有你。」

passages.original: “Thank you. You make me happy. I hope no fish will come along so great that he will prove us wrong.”
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你。你讓我高興。我希望唔會有咁大嘅魚出現,證明我哋錯喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你。你讓我高興。我希望不會有那麼大的魚出現,證明我們錯了。」

passages.original: “There is no such fish if you are still strong as you say.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你仲像你講嘅咁強壯,就冇嗰樣嘅魚。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你還像你說的那麼強壯,就沒有那樣的魚。」

passages.original: “I may not be as strong as I think,” the old man said. “But I know many tricks and I have resolution.”
passages.vernacular: 「我或者不像我想嘅咁強壯,」老人講。「但我知道許多竅門,而且我有決心。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也許不像我想的那麼強壯,」老人說。「但我知道許多竅門,而且我有決心。」

passages.original: “You ought to go to bed now so that you will be fresh in the morning. I will take the things back to the Terrace.”
passages.vernacular: 「你而家應該上床瞓覺,咁樣早晨才精神。我把嘢攞回露台餐館。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你現在應該上床睡覺,這樣早晨才精神。我把東西拿回露台餐館。」

passages.original: “Good night then. I will wake you in the morning.”
passages.vernacular: 「咁晚安。我早晨叫醒你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼晚安。我早晨叫醒你。」

passages.original: “You’re my alarm clock,” the boy said.
passages.vernacular: 「你係我嘅鬧鐘,」男孩講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是我的鬧鐘,」男孩說。

passages.original: “Age is my alarm clock,” the old man said. “Why do old men wake so early? Is it to have one longer day?”
passages.vernacular: 「年紀係我嘅鬧鐘,」老人講。「點解老人醒得咁早?係為了多一個長啲嘅白天嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「年紀是我的鬧鐘,」老人說。「為什麼老人醒得那麼早?是為了多一個長一點的白天嗎?」

passages.original: “I don’t know,” the boy said. “All I know is that young boys sleep late and hard.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道,」男孩講。「我只知道小細路瞓得又晚又沉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道,」男孩說。「我只知道小孩子睡得又晚又沉。」

passages.original: “I can remember it,” the old man said. “I’ll waken you in time.”
passages.vernacular: 「我記得,」老人講。「我會及時叫醒你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我記得,」老人說。「我會及時叫醒你。」

passages.original: “I do not like for him to waken me. It is as though I were inferior.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不鍾意佢叫醒我。好像我低人一等似嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不喜歡他叫醒我。好像我低人一等似的。」

passages.original: “I know.”
passages.vernacular: 「我知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道。」

passages.original: “Sleep well, old man.”
passages.vernacular: 「瞓好,老人家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「睡好,老人家。」

passages.original: The boy went out. They had eaten with no light on the table and the old man took off his trousers and went to bed in the dark. He rolled his trousers up to make a pillow, putting the newspaper inside them. He rolled himself in the blanket and slept on the other old newspapers that covered the springs of the bed.
passages.vernacular: 男孩出去喇。佢哋食飯時桌上冇點燈,老人脫掉長褲,喺黑暗中上咗床。佢把長褲捲起嚟當枕頭,把報紙塞喺裡面。佢用毯子裹住自己,瞓喺蓋住床彈簧嘅其他舊報紙上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩出去了。他們吃飯時桌上沒有點燈,老人脫掉長褲,在黑暗中上了床。他把長褲捲起來當枕頭,把報紙塞在裡面。他用毯子裹住自己,睡在蓋住床彈簧的其他舊報紙上。

passages.original: He was asleep in a short time and he dreamed of Africa when he was a boy and the long golden beaches and the white beaches, so white they hurt your eyes, and the high capes and the great brown mountains. He lived along that coast now every night and in his dreams he heard the surf roar and saw the native boats come riding through it. He smelled the tar and oakum of the deck as he slept and he smelled the smell of Africa that the land breeze brought at morning.
passages.vernacular: 佢好快就瞓住喇,夢見佢定係男孩時嘅非洲,長長嘅金色海灘同白色海灘,白得刺眼,高高嘅海角同棕色嘅大山。而家佢每天夜裡都生活喺嗰片海岸邊,喺夢中聽到浪濤怒吼,睇到土住嘅船乘住浪駛嚟。瞓夢中佢聞到甲板嘅柏油同麻絮嘅氣味,聞到早晨陸風帶嚟嘅非洲嘅氣味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他很快就睡著了,夢見他還是男孩時的非洲,長長的金色海灘和白色海灘,白得刺眼,高高的海角和棕色的大山。現在他每天夜裡都生活在那片海岸邊,在夢中聽到浪濤怒吼,看到土著的船乘著浪駛來。睡夢中他聞到甲板的柏油和麻絮的氣味,聞到早晨陸風帶來的非洲的氣味。

passages.original: Usually when he smelled the land breeze he woke up and dressed to go and wake the boy. But tonight the smell of the land breeze came very early and he knew it was too early in his dream and went on dreaming to see the white peaks of the Islands rising from the sea and then he dreamed of the different harbours and roadsteads of the Canary Islands.
passages.vernacular: 通常佢聞到陸風就醒嚟,穿好衣服去叫醒男孩。但今晚陸風嘅氣味嚟得好早,佢知道喺夢裡太早喇,就繼續做夢,睇到群島嘅白色山峰從海中升起,然後佢夢見加嗰利群島各個不同嘅港口同錨地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 通常他聞到陸風就醒來,穿好衣服去叫醒男孩。但今晚陸風的氣味來得很早,他知道在夢裡太早了,就繼續做夢,看到群島的白色山峰從海中升起,然後他夢見加那利群島各個不同的港口和錨地。

passages.original: He no longer dreamed of storms, nor of women, nor of great occurrences, nor of great fish, nor fights, nor contests of strength, nor of his wife. He only dreamed of places now and of the lions on the beach. They played like young cats in the dusk and he loved them as he loved the boy. He never dreamed about the boy. He simply woke, looked out the open door at the moon and unrolled his trousers and put them on. He urinated outside the shack and then went up the road to wake the boy. He was shivering with the morning cold. But he knew he would shiver himself warm and that soon he would be rowing.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔再夢見風暴,都不夢見女人,不夢見大事件,不夢見大魚,不夢見打鬥,不夢見比力氣,都不夢見佢嘅妻子。佢而家只夢見地方,同海灘上嘅獅子。牠哋喺暮色中像小貓一樣玩耍,佢愛牠哋,就像愛嗰個男孩一樣。佢從不夢見嗰個男孩。佢只係醒嚟,透過敞開嘅門睇住月亮,展開佢嘅長褲穿上。佢喺小屋外面小便,然後沿住路上去叫醒男孩。佢被早晨嘅寒冷凍得發抖。但佢知道,自己會抖到暖同,不久就要划船喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不再夢見風暴,也不夢見女人,不夢見大事件,不夢見大魚,不夢見打鬥,不夢見比力氣,也不夢見他的妻子。他現在只夢見地方,和海灘上的獅子。牠們在暮色中像小貓一樣玩耍,他愛牠們,就像愛那個男孩一樣。他從不夢見那個男孩。他只是醒來,透過敞開的門看著月亮,展開他的長褲穿上。他在小屋外面小便,然後沿著路上去叫醒男孩。他被早晨的寒冷凍得發抖。但他知道,自己會抖到暖和,不久就要划船了。

passages.original: The door of the house where the boy lived was unlocked and he opened it and walked in quietly with his bare feet. The boy was asleep on a cot in the first room and the old man could see him clearly with the light that came in from the dying moon. He took hold of one foot gently and held it until the boy woke and turned and looked at him. The old man nodded and the boy took his trousers from the chair by the bed and, sitting on the bed, pulled them on.
passages.vernacular: 男孩住嘅房子嘅門冇鎖,佢打開門,光住腳悄悄走進去。男孩瞓喺第一個房間嘅一張行軍床上,借住殘月嘅光,老人可以清楚地睇見佢。佢輕輕握住一隻腳,握住直到男孩醒嚟,轉身睇住佢。老人點點頭,男孩從床邊椅子上攞起佢嘅長褲,坐喺床上穿上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩住的房子的門沒鎖,他打開門,光著腳悄悄走進去。男孩睡在第一個房間的一張行軍床上,借著殘月的光,老人可以清楚地看見他。他輕輕握住一隻腳,握著直到男孩醒來,轉身看著他。老人點點頭,男孩從床邊椅子上拿起他的長褲,坐在床上穿上。

chapters.title: II. Out to Sea 出海

passages.original: The old man went out the door and the boy came after him. He was sleepy and the old man put his arm across his shoulders and said, “I am sorry.”
passages.vernacular: 老人走出門,男孩跟喺佢後面。佢睏倦,老人把手臂搭喺佢肩上,講:「對不起。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老人走出門,男孩跟在他後面。他睏倦,老人把手臂搭在他肩上,說:「對不起。」

passages.original: “Qu� va,” the boy said. “It is what a man must do.”
passages.vernacular: 「邊有嘅事,」男孩講。「呢個係男人必須做嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哪有的事,」男孩說。「這是男人必須做的。」

passages.original: They walked down the road to the old man’s shack and all along the road, in the dark, barefoot men were moving, carrying the masts of their boats.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋沿住路走向老人嘅小屋,一路上,喺黑暗中,赤腳嘅男人哋喺走動,扛住佢哋船嘅桅杆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們沿著路走向老人的小屋,一路上,在黑暗中,赤腳的男人們在走動,扛著他們船的桅杆。

passages.original: When they reached the old man’s shack the boy took the rolls of line in the basket and the harpoon and gaff and the old man carried the mast with the furled sail on his shoulder.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋到老人嘅小屋時,男孩攞起籃子裡嘅幾卷釣索、魚叉同魚鉤,老人扛起捲住帆嘅桅杆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們到老人的小屋時,男孩拿起籃子裡的幾卷釣索、魚叉和魚鉤,老人扛起捲著帆的桅杆。

passages.original: “Do you want coffee?” the boy asked.
passages.vernacular: 「你要咖啡嗎?」男孩問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你要咖啡嗎?」男孩問。

passages.original: “We’ll put the gear in the boat and then get some.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋先把裝備放到船上,然後去飲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們先把裝備放到船上,然後去喝。」

passages.original: They had coffee from condensed milk cans at an early morning place that served fishermen.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺一家為漁夫服務嘅清晨店裡,用煉乳罐飲咗咖啡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們在一家為漁夫服務的清晨店裡,用煉乳罐喝了咖啡。

passages.original: “How did you sleep old man?” the boy asked. He was waking up now although it was still hard for him to leave his sleep.
passages.vernacular: 「你瞓得點樣,老人家?」男孩問。佢而家醒過嚟喇,雖然仍好難離開瞓眠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你睡得怎樣,老人家?」男孩問。他現在醒過來了,雖然仍很難離開睡眠。

passages.original: “Very well, Manolin,” the old man said. “I feel confident today.”
passages.vernacular: 「好好,馬諾林,」老人講。「今日我覺得好有信心。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好,馬諾林,」老人說。「今天我覺得很有信心。」

passages.original: “So do I,” the boy said. “Now I must get your sardines and mine and your fresh baits. He brings our gear himself. He never wants anyone to carry anything.”
passages.vernacular: 「我都係,」男孩講。「而家我必須去攞你嘅同我嘅沙丁魚,仲有你嘅新鮮餌。佢自己把我哋嘅裝備帶嚟。佢從唔想讓任何人搬任何嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也是,」男孩說。「現在我必須去拿你的和我的沙丁魚,還有你的新鮮餌。他自己把我們的裝備帶來。他從不想讓任何人搬任何東西。」

passages.original: “We’re different,” the old man said. “I let you carry things when you were five years old.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋不同,」老人講。「你五歲時我就讓你搬嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們不同,」老人說。「你五歲時我就讓你搬東西。」

passages.original: “I know it,” the boy said. “I’ll be right back. Have another coffee. We have credit here.”
passages.vernacular: 「我知道,」男孩講。「我即刻回嚟。再飲一杯咖啡。我哋喺呢度有賒賬。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道,」男孩說。「我馬上回來。再喝一杯咖啡。我們在這裡有賒賬。」

passages.original: He walked off, bare-footed on the coral rocks, to the ice house where the baits were stored.
passages.vernacular: 佢赤腳走過珊瑚石,走向存放餌嘅冰屋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他赤腳走過珊瑚石,走向存放餌的冰屋。

passages.original: The old man drank his coffee slowly. It was all he would have all day and he knew that he should take it. For a long time now eating had bored him and he never carried a lunch. He had a bottle of water in the bow of the skiff and that was all he needed for the day.
passages.vernacular: 老人慢慢飲住咖啡。呢個係佢一整天嘅全部食物,佢知道應該飲。好長時間以來,食嘢讓佢厭煩,佢從不帶午飯。佢喺小艇船頭有一瓶水,嗰個就係佢一天所需要嘅全部。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老人慢慢喝著咖啡。這是他一整天的全部食物,他知道應該喝。很長時間以來,吃東西讓他厭煩,他從不帶午飯。他在小艇船頭有一瓶水,那就是他一天所需要的全部。

passages.original: The boy was back now with the sardines and the two baits wrapped in a newspaper and they went down the trail to the skiff, feeling the pebbled sand under their feet, and lifted the skiff and slid her into the water.
passages.vernacular: 男孩而家帶住沙丁魚同用報紙包住嘅兩條餌回嚟喇,佢哋沿住小徑走向小艇,腳下感覺到鋪滿卵石嘅沙子,把小艇抬起嚟,滑進水裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩現在帶著沙丁魚和用報紙包著的兩條餌回來了,他們沿著小徑走向小艇,腳下感覺到鋪滿卵石的沙子,把小艇抬起來,滑進水裡。

passages.original: “Good luck old man.”
passages.vernacular: 「祝你好運,老人家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「祝你好運,老人家。」

passages.original: “Good luck,” the old man said. He fitted the rope lashings of the oars onto the thole pins and, leaning forward against the thrust of the blades in the water, he began to row out of the harbour in the dark. There were other boats from the other beaches going out to sea and the old man heard the dip and push of their oars even though he could not see them now the moon was below the hills.
passages.vernacular: 「祝你好運,」老人講。佢把槳嘅繩圈套喺槳栓上,身體前傾,頂住槳葉喺水中嘅推力,喺黑暗中開始把船划出港口。仲有別嘅海灘出嚟嘅其他船出海,老人聽到佢哋嘅槳入水同推動嘅聲音,雖然而家月亮已落到山後,佢睇唔見佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「祝你好運,」老人說。他把槳的繩圈套在槳栓上,身體前傾,頂著槳葉在水中的推力,在黑暗中開始把船划出港口。還有別的海灘出來的其他船出海,老人聽到它們的槳入水和推動的聲音,雖然現在月亮已落到山後,他看不見它們。

passages.original: Sometimes someone would speak in a boat. But most of the boats were silent except for the dip of the oars. They spread apart after they were out of the mouth of the harbour and each one headed for the part of the ocean where he hoped to find fish. The old man knew he was going far out and he left the smell of the land behind and rowed out into the clean early morning smell of the ocean. He saw the phosphorescence of the Gulf weed in the water as he rowed over the part of the ocean that the fishermen called the great well because there was a sudden deep of seven hundred fathoms where all sorts of fish congregated because of the swirl the current made against the steep walls of the floor of the ocean. Here there were concentrations of shrimp and bait fish and sometimes schools of squid in the deepest holes and these rose close to the surface at night where all the wandering fish fed on them.
passages.vernacular: 有時船上有人講話。但大多數船除咗槳入水嘅聲音外都好安靜。出港口之後佢哋分散開,每條船駛向佢希望能找到魚嘅嗰部分海洋。老人知道佢要遠遠地出去,佢把陸地嘅氣味拋喺後面,划進清新嘅清晨海洋氣味裡。佢划過漁夫哋稱為大井嘅嗰片海域,嗰度突然深達七百噚,各種魚因洋流衝擊海底陡壁產生嘅漩渦而聚集,佢睇到水中馬尾藻嘅磷光。呢度聚集住蝦同餌魚,喺最深嘅洞裡有時仲有成群嘅魷魚,佢哋夜裡浮到靠近水面嘅地方,所有遊蕩嘅魚都以佢哋為食。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時船上有人說話。但大多數船除了槳入水的聲音外都很安靜。出港口之後它們分散開,每條船駛向他希望能找到魚的那部分海洋。老人知道他要遠遠地出去,他把陸地的氣味拋在後面,划進清新的清晨海洋氣味裡。他划過漁夫們稱為大井的那片海域,那裡突然深達七百噚,各種魚因洋流衝擊海底陡壁產生的漩渦而聚集,他看到水中馬尾藻的磷光。這裡聚集著蝦和餌魚,在最深的洞裡有時還有成群的魷魚,它們夜裡浮到靠近水面的地方,所有遊蕩的魚都以它們為食。

passages.original: In the dark the old man could feel the morning coming and as he rowed he heard the trembling sound as flying fish left the water and the hissing that their stiff set wings made as they soared away in the darkness. He was very fond of flying fish as they were his principal friends on the ocean. He was sorry for the birds, especially the small delicate dark terns that were always flying and looking and almost never finding, and he thought, “The birds have a harder life than we do except for the robber birds and the heavy strong ones. Why did they make birds so delicate and fine as those sea swallows when the ocean can be so cruel? She is kind and very beautiful. But she can be so cruel and it comes so suddenly and such birds that fly, dipping and hunting, with their small sad voices are made too delicately for the sea.”
passages.vernacular: 喺黑暗中,老人能感覺到早晨正在到來,佢划住船,聽到飛魚離開水面時顫抖嘅聲音,同牠哋僵直嘅翅膀喺黑暗中飛走時發出嘅嘶嘶聲。佢好鍾意飛魚,因為牠哋係佢喺海上主要嘅朋友。佢為鳥感到難過,特別係嗰啲小巧嬌弱嘅深色燕鷗,牠哋總是喺飛、喺找,幾乎從來找唔到,佢想:「鳥嘅生活比我哋更艱難,除咗強盜鳥同強壯嘅重鳥。海洋可以咁殘酷,點解把鳥造得像嗰啲海燕咁嬌弱精緻?佢係仁慈而好美麗嘅。但佢可以咁殘酷,而且嚟得咁突然,嗰啲飛翔住、俯衝獵食、發出細小悲傷叫聲嘅鳥,造得對海來講太嬌弱喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在黑暗中,老人能感覺到早晨正在到來,他划著船,聽到飛魚離開水面時顫抖的聲音,和牠們僵直的翅膀在黑暗中飛走時發出的嘶嘶聲。他非常喜歡飛魚,因為牠們是他在海上主要的朋友。他為鳥感到難過,特別是那些小巧嬌弱的深色燕鷗,牠們總是在飛、在找,幾乎從來找不到,他想:「鳥的生活比我們更艱難,除了強盜鳥和強壯的重鳥。海洋可以那麼殘酷,為什麼把鳥造得像那些海燕那麼嬌弱精緻?她是仁慈而非常美麗的。但她可以那麼殘酷,而且來得那麼突然,那些飛翔著、俯衝獵食、發出細小悲傷叫聲的鳥,造得對海來說太嬌弱了。」

passages.original: He always thought of the sea as la mar which is what people call her in Spanish when they love her. Sometimes those who love her say bad things of her but they are always said as though she were a woman. Some of the younger fishermen, those who used buoys as floats for their lines and had motorboats, bought when the shark livers had brought much money, spoke of her as el mar which is masculine. They spoke of her as a contestant or a place or even an enemy. But the old man always thought of her as feminine and as something that gave or withheld great favours, and if she did wild or wicked things it was because she could not help them. The moon affects her as it does a woman, he thought.
passages.vernacular: 佢總是把海想成「拉馬爾」,呢個係西班牙語中人哋愛佢時對佢嘅稱呼。有時愛佢嘅人都講佢嘅壞話,但總是像喺講一個女人。啲較年輕嘅漁夫,嗰啲用浮標做釣線浮子、有機動船嘅人,係鯊魚肝賺咗大錢時買嘅,稱佢為「埃爾馬爾」,係陽性。佢哋把佢當作對手、一個地方,甚至敵人。但老人總是把佢想成女性,想成一個畀予或扣留巨大恩惠嘅嘢,如果佢做出狂暴或邪惡嘅事,嗰個係因為佢身不由己。月亮影響佢,就像影響一個女人一樣,佢想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他總是把海想成「拉馬爾」,這是西班牙語中人們愛她時對她的稱呼。有時愛她的人也說她的壞話,但總是像在說一個女人。一些較年輕的漁夫,那些用浮標做釣線浮子、有機動船的人,是鯊魚肝賺了大錢時買的,稱她為「埃爾馬爾」,是陽性。他們把她當作對手、一個地方,甚至敵人。但老人總是把她想成女性,想成一個給予或扣留巨大恩惠的東西,如果她做出狂暴或邪惡的事,那是因為她身不由己。月亮影響她,就像影響一個女人一樣,他想。

passages.original: He was rowing steadily and it was no effort for him since he kept well within his speed and the surface of the ocean was flat except for the occasional swirls of the current. He was letting the current do a third of the work and as it started to be light he saw he was already further out than he had hoped to be at this hour.
passages.vernacular: 佢穩定地划住船,毫不費力,因為佢保持喺佢速度範圍之內,海面係平嘅,只有偶爾洋流嘅漩渦。佢讓洋流做咗三分之一嘅工作,天開始亮時,佢睇到自己已經比佢希望喺呢個時刻到達嘅地方更遠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他穩定地划著船,毫不費力,因為他保持在他速度範圍之內,海面是平的,只有偶爾洋流的漩渦。他讓洋流做了三分之一的工作,天開始亮時,他看到自己已經比他希望在這個時刻到達的地方更遠了。

passages.original: I worked the deep wells for a week and did nothing, he thought. Today I’ll work out where the schools of bonita and albacore are and maybe there will be a big one with them.
passages.vernacular: 我喺深井作業咗一個星期,乜嘢都冇,佢想。今日我要去找鰹魚同長鰭金槍魚群喺邊度,或者牠哋中間有一條大嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在深井作業了一個星期,什麼也沒有,他想。今天我要去找鰹魚和長鰭金槍魚群在哪裡,也許牠們中間有一條大的。

passages.original: Before it was really light he had his baits out and was drifting with the current. One bait was down forty fathoms. The second was at seventy-five and the third and fourth were down in the blue water at one hundred and one hundred and twenty-five fathoms. Each bait hung head down with the shank of the hook inside the bait fish, tied and sewed solid and all the projecting part of the hook, the curve and the point, was covered with fresh sardines. Each sardine was hooked through both eyes so that they made a half-garland on the projecting steel. There was no part of the hook that a great fish could feel which was not sweet smelling and good tasting.
passages.vernacular: 天仲冇真正亮,佢就把餌放下去,隨洋流漂流。一條餌喺四十噚深。第二條喺七十五噚,第三同第四條喺藍水中一百同一百二十五噚。每條餌頭朝下掛住,魚鉤嘅柄喺餌魚裡面,綁緊縫牢,魚鉤所有突出嘅部分,彎曲同尖端,都用新鮮沙丁魚蓋住。每條沙丁魚嘅兩隻眼睛都被鉤穿,使牠哋喺突出嘅鋼上形成半個花環。魚鉤上冇一個大魚能感覺到嘅部分,唔係氣味香甜、味道好嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天還沒有真正亮,他就把餌放下去,隨洋流漂流。一條餌在四十噚深。第二條在七十五噚,第三和第四條在藍水中一百和一百二十五噚。每條餌頭朝下掛著,魚鉤的柄在餌魚裡面,綁緊縫牢,魚鉤所有突出的部分,彎曲和尖端,都用新鮮沙丁魚蓋住。每條沙丁魚的兩隻眼睛都被鉤穿,使牠們在突出的鋼上形成半個花環。魚鉤上沒有一個大魚能感覺到的部分,不是氣味香甜、味道好的。

passages.original: The boy had given him two fresh small tunas, or albacores, which hung on the two deepest lines like plummets and, on the others, he had a big blue runner and a yellow jack that had been used before; but they were in good condition still and had the excellent sardines to give them scent and attractiveness. Each line, as thick around as a big pencil, was looped onto a green-sapped stick so that any pull or touch on the bait would make the stick dip and each line had two forty-fathom coils which could be made fast to the other spare coils so that, if it were necessary, a fish could take out over three hundred fathoms of line.
passages.vernacular: 男孩畀咗佢兩條新鮮嘅小金槍魚,或叫長鰭金槍魚,掛喺兩條最深嘅線上像鉛錘,而喺其他線上,佢有一條大藍鰺同一條黃鰺,以前用過;但仍然狀況良好,有極好嘅沙丁魚畀牠哋提供氣味同吸引力。每根線,粗如一支大鉛筆,套喺一根綠嫩樹枝上,咁樣餌上嘅任何一拉或一碰都會使樹枝下沉,每根線有兩個四十噚嘅線圈,可以同其他備用線圈繫牢,咁樣如果必要,一條魚可以拉出三百多噚線。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩給了他兩條新鮮的小金槍魚,或叫長鰭金槍魚,掛在兩條最深的線上像鉛錘,而在其他線上,他有一條大藍鰺和一條黃鰺,以前用過;但仍然狀況良好,有極好的沙丁魚給牠們提供氣味和吸引力。每根線,粗如一支大鉛筆,套在一根綠嫩樹枝上,這樣餌上的任何一拉或一碰都會使樹枝下沉,每根線有兩個四十噚的線圈,可以和其他備用線圈繫牢,這樣如果必要,一條魚可以拉出三百多噚線。

passages.original: Now the man watched the dip of the three sticks over the side of the skiff and rowed gently to keep the lines straight up and down and at their proper depths. It was quite light and any moment now the sun would rise.
passages.vernacular: 而家老人注視住小艇側邊三根樹枝嘅下沉,輕輕地划船,保持線上下垂直,喺合適嘅深度。天已經好亮喇,隨時太陽就要升起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在老人注視著小艇側邊三根樹枝的下沉,輕輕地划船,保持線上下垂直,在合適的深度。天已經很亮了,隨時太陽就要升起。

passages.original: The sun rose thinly from the sea and the old man could see the other boats, low on the water and well in toward the shore, spread out across the current. Then the sun was brighter and the glare came on the water and then, as it rose clear, the flat sea sent it back at his eyes so that it hurt sharply and he rowed without looking into it. He looked down into the water and watched the lines that went straight down into the dark of the water. He kept them straighter than anyone did, so that at each level in the darkness of the stream there would be a bait waiting exactly where he wished it to be for any fish that swam there. Others let them drift with the current and sometimes they were at sixty fathoms when the fishermen thought they were at a hundred.
passages.vernacular: 太陽從海上淡淡地升起,老人可以睇到其他船,低低地靠喺水面,遠遠地喺近岸處,散佈喺洋流上。然後太陽更亮喇,炫光照到水面,然後,當佢完全升起,平坦嘅海面把佢反射回佢嘅眼睛,使眼睛刺痛,佢不睇住佢划船。佢往下望住水裡,睇住直直沉入水中黑暗處嘅線。佢把佢哋保持得比任何人都更直,咁樣喺洋流黑暗中每個深度都有一條餌,恰好等喺佢希望嘅地方,等待游到嗰度嘅任何魚。別人讓佢哋隨洋流漂流,有時漁夫哋以為喺一百噚時,佢哋實際只喺六十噚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太陽從海上淡淡地升起,老人可以看到其他船,低低地靠在水面,遠遠地在近岸處,散佈在洋流上。然後太陽更亮了,炫光照到水面,然後,當它完全升起,平坦的海面把它反射回他的眼睛,使眼睛刺痛,他不看著它划船。他往下望著水裡,看著直直沉入水中黑暗處的線。他把它們保持得比任何人都更直,這樣在洋流黑暗中每個深度都有一條餌,恰好等在他希望的地方,等待游到那裡的任何魚。別人讓它們隨洋流漂流,有時漁夫們以為在一百噚時,它們實際只在六十噚。

passages.original: But, he thought, I keep them with precision. Only I have no luck any more. But who knows? Maybe today. Every day is a new day. It is better to be lucky. But I would rather be exact. Then when luck comes you are ready.
passages.vernacular: 但係,佢想,我讓佢哋精確。只係我唔再有運氣。但邊個知道呢?或者今日。每一天都係新嘅一天。有運氣更好。但我寧願準確。咁樣運氣嚟嘅時候你就準備好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,他想,我讓它們精確。只是我不再有運氣。但誰知道呢?也許今天。每一天都是新的一天。有運氣更好。但我寧願準確。這樣運氣來的時候你就準備好了。

passages.original: The sun was two hours higher now and it did not hurt his eyes so much to look into the east. There were only three boats in sight now and they showed very low and far inshore.
passages.vernacular: 太陽而家高咗兩小時,睇向東方不咁刺痛佢嘅眼睛喇。而家只睇到三條船,佢哋顯得好低,遠喺近岸處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太陽現在高了兩小時,看向東方不那麼刺痛他的眼睛了。現在只看到三條船,它們顯得很低,遠在近岸處。

passages.original: All my life the early sun has hurt my eyes, he thought. Yet they are still good. In the evening I can look straight into it without getting the blackness. It has more force in the evening too. But in the morning it is painful.
passages.vernacular: 我一輩子,早晨嘅太陽都傷我嘅眼睛,佢想。然而佢哋仍然係好嘅。晚上我可以直視佢而唔會睇見黑暗。傍晚佢嘅力量都更大。但早晨係痛苦嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一輩子,早晨的太陽都傷我的眼睛,他想。然而它們仍然是好的。晚上我可以直視它而不會看見黑暗。傍晚它的力量也更大。但早晨是痛苦的。

passages.original: Just then he saw a man-of-war bird with his long black wings circling in the sky ahead of him. He made a quick drop, slanting down on his back-swept wings, and then circled again.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢陣,佢睇到一隻軍艦鳥張住長長嘅黑翅膀,喺前方天空盤旋。牠急速下降,翅膀向後掠斜住俯衝,然後又盤旋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這時,他看到一隻軍艦鳥張著長長的黑翅膀,在前方天空盤旋。牠急速下降,翅膀向後掠斜著俯衝,然後又盤旋。

passages.original: “He’s got something,” the old man said aloud. “He’s not just looking.”
passages.vernacular: 「牠發現咗乜嘢,」老人大聲講。「牠不只係喺睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「牠發現了什麼,」老人大聲說。「牠不只是在看。」

passages.original: He rowed slowly and steadily toward where the bird was circling. He did not hurry and he kept his lines straight up and down. But he crowded the current a little so that he was still fishing correctly though faster than he would have fished if he was not trying to use the bird.
passages.vernacular: 佢緩慢而穩定地朝鳥盤旋嘅地方划去。佢不急,保持佢嘅線上下垂直。但佢稍稍逼近洋流,咁樣佢仍然喺正確地捕魚,雖然比不利用嗰隻鳥時更快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他緩慢而穩定地朝鳥盤旋的地方划去。他不急,保持他的線上下垂直。但他稍稍逼近洋流,這樣他仍然在正確地捕魚,雖然比不利用那隻鳥時更快。

passages.original: The bird went higher in the air and circled again, his wings motionless. Then he dove suddenly and the old man saw flying fish spurt out of the water and sail desperately over the surface.
passages.vernacular: 鳥飛得更高,又盤旋,翅膀一動不動。然後牠突然俯衝,老人睇到飛魚從水中躍出,拚命滑翔過水面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鳥飛得更高,又盤旋,翅膀一動不動。然後牠突然俯衝,老人看到飛魚從水中躍出,拚命滑翔過水面。

passages.original: “Dolphin,” the old man said aloud. “Big dolphin.”
passages.vernacular: 「鬼頭刀,」老人大聲講。「大鬼頭刀。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「鬼頭刀,」老人大聲說。「大鬼頭刀。」

passages.original: He shipped his oars and brought a small line from under the bow. It had a wire leader and a medium-sized hook and he baited it with one of the sardines. He let it go over the side and then made it fast to a ring bolt in the stern. Then he baited another line and left it coiled in the shade of the bow. He went back to rowing and to watching the long-winged black bird who was working, now, low over the water.
passages.vernacular: 佢收起槳,從船頭下攞出一根細線。佢有一條鋼絲導線同一個中等大小嘅魚鉤,佢用一條沙丁魚上餌。佢把佢放到船舷外,然後把佢繫喺船尾嘅一個環釘上。然後佢喺另一根線上上咗餌,把佢盤好留喺船頭嘅陰影裡。佢回去划船,觀察嗰隻長翼嘅黑鳥,牠而家正低低地喺水面上忙碌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他收起槳,從船頭下拿出一根細線。它有一條鋼絲導線和一個中等大小的魚鉤,他用一條沙丁魚上餌。他把它放到船舷外,然後把它繫在船尾的一個環釘上。然後他在另一根線上上了餌,把它盤好留在船頭的陰影裡。他回去划船,觀察那隻長翼的黑鳥,牠現在正低低地在水面上忙碌。

passages.original: As he watched the bird dipped again slanting his wings for the dive and then swinging them wildly and ineffectually as he followed the flying fish. The old man could see the slight bulge in the water that the big dolphin raised as they followed the escaping fish. The dolphin were cutting through the water below the flight of the fish and would be in the water, driving at speed, when the fish dropped. It is a big school of dolphin, he thought. They are wide spread and the flying fish have little chance. The bird has no chance. The flying fish are too big for him and they go too fast.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇住,鳥又俯衝,傾斜住翅膀俯衝,然後喺追逐飛魚時瘋狂而徒勞地拍動翅膀。老人可以睇到大鬼頭刀追逐逃跑嘅魚時喺水中掀起嘅輕微隆起。鬼頭刀喺飛魚飛行嘅下方切開水面,喺魚落下時,會喺水中,高速衝刺。呢個係一大群鬼頭刀,佢想。牠哋散得好開,飛魚幾乎冇機會。鳥冇機會。飛魚對牠太大,又飛得太快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看著,鳥又俯衝,傾斜著翅膀俯衝,然後在追逐飛魚時瘋狂而徒勞地拍動翅膀。老人可以看到大鬼頭刀追逐逃跑的魚時在水中掀起的輕微隆起。鬼頭刀在飛魚飛行的下方切開水面,在魚落下時,會在水中,高速衝刺。這是一大群鬼頭刀,他想。牠們散得很開,飛魚幾乎沒有機會。鳥沒有機會。飛魚對牠太大,又飛得太快。

passages.original: He watched the flying fish burst out again and again and the ineffectual movements of the bird. That school has gotten away from me, he thought. They are moving out too fast and too far. But perhaps I will pick up a stray and perhaps my big fish is around them. My big fish must be somewhere.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇住飛魚一次又一次地衝出水面,同鳥徒勞嘅動作。嗰群魚從我身邊溜走喇,佢想。牠哋移動得太快太遠。但或者我會撿到一條落單嘅,或者我嘅大魚就喺牠哋周圍。我嘅大魚一定喺某處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看著飛魚一次又一次地衝出水面,和鳥徒勞的動作。那群魚從我身邊溜走了,他想。牠們移動得太快太遠。但也許我會撿到一條落單的,也許我的大魚就在牠們周圍。我的大魚一定在某處。

passages.original: The clouds over the land now rose like mountains and the coast was only a long green line with the gray blue hills behind it. The water was a dark blue now, so dark that it was almost purple. As he looked down into it he saw the red sifting of the plankton in the dark water and the strange light the sun made now. He watched his lines to see them go straight down out of sight into the water and he was happy to see so much plankton because it meant fish. The strange light the sun made in the water, now that the sun was higher, meant good weather and so did the shape of the clouds over the land. But the bird was almost out of sight now and nothing showed on the surface of the water but some patches of yellow, sun-bleached Sargasso weed and the purple, formalized, iridescent, gelatinous bladder of a Portuguese man-of-war floating close beside the boat. It turned on its side and then righted itself. It floated cheerfully as a bubble with its long deadly purple filaments trailing a yard behind it in the water.
passages.vernacular: 陸地上空嘅雲而家像山一樣升起,海岸只係一條長長嘅綠線,後面係灰藍嘅山丘。水而家係深藍色,深得幾乎係紫色。佢往下睇時,睇到黑水中浮游生物嘅紅色篩動,同太陽而家製造嘅奇異光線。佢睇住佢嘅線直直沉入水中睇唔見,佢睇到咁多浮游生物好高興,因為嗰意味住有魚。而家太陽更高喇,太陽喺水中製造嘅奇異光線,意味住好天氣,陸地上空雲嘅形狀都係。但鳥而家幾乎睇唔見喇,水面上乜嘢都冇,只有幾片黃色嘅、被太陽曬白嘅馬尾藻,同一個紫色嘅、形狀規整嘅、虹彩嘅、膠質嘅僧帽水母氣囊,漂喺船旁邊好近嘅地方。佢側過身,然後又擺正。佢像個氣泡一樣歡快地漂浮,長長嘅致命嘅紫色觸鬚喺水中拖喺身後一碼遠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 陸地上空的雲現在像山一樣升起,海岸只是一條長長的綠線,後面是灰藍的山丘。水現在是深藍色,深得幾乎是紫色。他往下看時,看到黑水中浮游生物的紅色篩動,和太陽現在製造的奇異光線。他看著他的線直直沉入水中看不見,他看到那麼多浮游生物很高興,因為那意味著有魚。現在太陽更高了,太陽在水中製造的奇異光線,意味著好天氣,陸地上空雲的形狀也是。但鳥現在幾乎看不見了,水面上什麼也沒有,只有幾片黃色的、被太陽曬白的馬尾藻,和一個紫色的、形狀規整的、虹彩的、膠質的僧帽水母氣囊,漂在船旁邊很近的地方。它側過身,然後又擺正。它像個氣泡一樣歡快地漂浮,長長的致命的紫色觸鬚在水中拖在身後一碼遠。

passages.original: “Agua mala,” the man said. “You whore.”
passages.vernacular: 「毒水母,」老人講。「你呢婊子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「毒水母,」老人說。「你這婊子。」

passages.original: From where he swung lightly against his oars he looked down into the water and saw the tiny fish that were coloured like the trailing filaments and swam between them and under the small shade the bubble made as it drifted. They were immune to its poison. But men were not and when some of the filaments would catch on a line and rest there slimy and purple while the old man was working a fish, he would have welts and sores on his arms and hands of the sort that poison ivy or poison oak can give. But these poisonings from the agua mala came quickly and struck like a whiplash.
passages.vernacular: 佢輕輕靠喺槳上搖晃,往水裡睇,睇到有微小嘅魚,顏色同拖住嘅觸鬚一樣,喺觸鬚之間和氣泡漂動時產生嘅小小陰影下游動。牠哋對佢嘅毒免疫。但人唔係,當啲觸鬚纏喺線上,黏滑而紫色地停喺嗰度,而老人正在對付一條魚時,佢嘅手臂同手上會起腫塊同潰瘍,就像毒藤或毒櫟引起嘅嗰種。但呢種毒水母嘅中毒嚟得好快,像鞭子一樣抽嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他輕輕靠在槳上搖晃,往水裡看,看到有微小的魚,顏色與拖著的觸鬚一樣,在觸鬚之間和氣泡漂動時產生的小小陰影下游動。牠們對它的毒免疫。但人不是,當一些觸鬚纏在線上,黏滑而紫色地停在那裡,而老人正在對付一條魚時,他的手臂和手上會起腫塊和潰瘍,就像毒藤或毒櫟引起的那種。但這種毒水母的中毒來得很快,像鞭子一樣抽來。

passages.original: The iridescent bubbles were beautiful. But they were the falsest thing in the sea and the old man loved to see the big sea turtles eating them. The turtles saw them, approached them from the front, then shut their eyes so they were completely carapaced and ate them filaments and all. The old man loved to see the turtles eat them and he loved to walk on them on the beach after a storm and hear them pop when he stepped on them with the horny soles of his feet.
passages.vernacular: 虹彩嘅氣泡係美麗嘅。但佢哋係海裡最虛假嘅嘢,老人鍾意睇大海龜食佢哋。海龜睇到佢哋,從前面靠近,然後閉上眼睛,咁樣完全被背甲保護住,連同觸鬚一起食掉。老人鍾意睇海龜食佢哋,佢鍾意暴風雨後喺海灘上走過佢哋,用佢角質嘅腳底踩上去,聽佢哋啪嘅一聲爆開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 虹彩的氣泡是美麗的。但它們是海裡最虛假的東西,老人喜歡看大海龜吃它們。海龜看到它們,從前面靠近,然後閉上眼睛,這樣完全被背甲保護著,連同觸鬚一起吃掉。老人喜歡看海龜吃它們,他喜歡暴風雨後在海灘上走過它們,用他角質的腳底踩上去,聽它們啪的一聲爆開。

passages.original: He loved green turtles and hawks-bills with their elegance and speed and their great value and he had a friendly contempt for the huge, stupid loggerheads, yellow in their armour-plating, strange in their love-making, and happily eating the Portuguese men-of-war with their eyes shut.
passages.vernacular: 佢鍾意綠海龜同玳瑁,牠哋優雅、敏捷,又好值錢,而佢對嗰啲巨大、愚蠢嘅蠵龜有一種友好嘅輕蔑,牠哋嘅甲殼係黃色嘅,交配方式奇怪,閉住眼睛快樂地食僧帽水母。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他喜歡綠海龜和玳瑁,牠們優雅、敏捷,又很值錢,而他對那些巨大、愚蠢的蠵龜有一種友好的輕蔑,牠們的甲殼是黃色的,交配方式奇怪,閉著眼睛快樂地吃僧帽水母。

passages.original: He had no mysticism about turtles although he had gone in turtle boats for many years. He was sorry for them all, even the great trunk backs that were as long as the skiff and weighed a ton. Most people are heartless about turtles because a turtle’s heart will beat for hours after he has been cut up and butchered. But the old man thought, I have such a heart too and my feet and hands are like theirs. He ate the white eggs to give himself strength. He ate them all through May to be strong in September and October for the truly big fish.
passages.vernacular: 佢對海龜冇神秘嘅想法,雖然佢多年嚟乘海龜船出海。佢為牠哋全都難過,甚至嗰啲同小艇一樣長、重一噸嘅大棱皮龜。大多數人對海龜好無情,因為海龜嘅心喺被切開、屠宰後仲會跳動幾個小時。但老人想,我都有咁樣嘅心,我嘅腳同手像牠哋嘅。佢食白色嘅龜蛋畀自己力量。佢整個五月都食,好喺九月同十月為真正嘅大魚保持強壯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他對海龜沒有神秘的想法,雖然他多年來乘海龜船出海。他為牠們全都難過,甚至那些和小艇一樣長、重一噸的大棱皮龜。大多數人對海龜很無情,因為海龜的心在被切開、屠宰後還會跳動幾個小時。但老人想,我也有這樣的心,我的腳和手像牠們的。他吃白色的龜蛋給自己力量。他整個五月都吃,好在九月和十月為真正的大魚保持強壯。

passages.original: He also drank a cup of shark liver oil each day from the big drum in the shack where many of the fishermen kept their gear. It was there for all fishermen who wanted it. Most fishermen hated the taste. But it was no worse than getting up at the hours that they rose and it was very good against all colds and grippes and it was good for the eyes.
passages.vernacular: 佢仲每天飲一杯鯊魚肝油,從小屋裡大桶中取,許多漁夫把佢哋嘅裝備放喺嗰度。佢喺嗰兒供所有想要嘅漁夫使用。大多數漁夫討厭嗰味道。但佢不比佢哋起床嘅時刻更壞,而且佢對所有感冒同流感好有效,對眼睛都好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他還每天喝一杯鯊魚肝油,從小屋裡大桶中取,許多漁夫把他們的裝備放在那裡。它在那兒供所有想要的漁夫使用。大多數漁夫討厭那味道。但它不比他們起床的時刻更壞,而且它對所有感冒和流感非常有效,對眼睛也好。

passages.original: Now the old man looked up and saw that the bird was circling again.
passages.vernacular: 而家老人抬頭睇,睇到鳥又喺盤旋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在老人抬頭看,看到鳥又在盤旋。

passages.original: “He’s found fish,” he said aloud. No flying fish broke the surface and there was no scattering of bait fish. But as the old man watched, a small tuna rose in the air, turned and dropped head first into the water. The tuna shone silver in the sun and after he had dropped back into the water another and another rose and they were jumping in all directions, churning the water and leaping in long jumps after the bait. They were circling it and driving it.
passages.vernacular: 「牠發現魚喇,」佢大聲講。冇飛魚躍出水面,都冇餌魚四散。但老人睇住,一條小金槍魚躍入空中,轉身,頭朝下落進水裡。金槍魚喺陽光下閃住銀光,牠落回水中後,另一條又一條躍起,牠哋向各個方向跳躍,攪動水面,喺追逐餌魚時作長長嘅跳躍。牠哋喺圍住牠,追趕牠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「牠發現魚了,」他大聲說。沒有飛魚躍出水面,也沒有餌魚四散。但老人看著,一條小金槍魚躍入空中,轉身,頭朝下落進水裡。金槍魚在陽光下閃著銀光,牠落回水中後,另一條又一條躍起,牠們向各個方向跳躍,攪動水面,在追逐餌魚時作長長的跳躍。牠們在圍著牠,追趕牠。

passages.original: If they don’t travel too fast I will get into them, the old man thought, and he watched the school working the water white and the bird now dropping and dipping into the bait fish that were forced to the surface in their panic.
passages.vernacular: 如果牠哋不走得太快,我就能趕上牠哋,老人想,佢睇住魚群把水攪成白色,鳥而家俯衝,啄向因驚慌被迫到水面嘅餌魚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果牠們不走得太快,我就能趕上牠們,老人想,他看著魚群把水攪成白色,鳥現在俯衝,啄向因驚慌被迫到水面的餌魚。

passages.original: “The bird is a great help,” the old man said. Just then the stern line came taut under his foot, where he had kept a loop of the line, and he dropped his oars and felt the weight of the small tuna’s shivering pull as he held the line firm and commenced to haul it in. The shivering increased as he pulled in and he could see the blue back of the fish in the water and the gold of his sides before he swung him over the side and into the boat. He lay in the stern in the sun, compact and bullet shaped, his big, unintelligent eyes staring as he thumped his life out against the planking of the boat with the quick shivering strokes of his neat, fast-moving tail. The old man hit him on the head for kindness and kicked him, his body still shuddering, under the shade of the stern.
passages.vernacular: 「鳥幫咗大忙,」老人講。就喺呢陣,船尾嘅線喺佢腳下繃緊喇,佢喺腳下留咗一個線圈,佢放下槳,感到小金槍魚顫抖拉扯嘅重量,佢穩穩握住線,開始往上拉。佢往上拉時顫抖加劇,佢能喺水中睇到魚嘅藍色背部同兩側嘅金色,然後佢把牠甩過船舷,進咗船。牠躺喺船尾陽光下,緊湊、子彈形,大而無神嘅眼睛瞪住,牠整齊、快速擺動嘅尾巴以快速顫抖嘅拍打,把生命拍盡喺船板上。老人出於仁慈打咗牠嘅頭,用腳把牠踢進船尾嘅陰影裡,牠嘅身體仍喺顫抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「鳥幫了大忙,」老人說。就在這時,船尾的線在他腳下繃緊了,他在腳下留了一個線圈,他放下槳,感到小金槍魚顫抖拉扯的重量,他穩穩握住線,開始往上拉。他往上拉時顫抖加劇,他能在水中看到魚的藍色背部和兩側的金色,然後他把牠甩過船舷,進了船。牠躺在船尾陽光下,緊湊、子彈形,大而無神的眼睛瞪著,牠整齊、快速擺動的尾巴以快速顫抖的拍打,把生命拍盡在船板上。老人出於仁慈打了牠的頭,用腳把牠踢進船尾的陰影裡,牠的身體仍在顫抖。

passages.original: “Albacore,” he said aloud. “He’ll make a beautiful bait. He’ll weigh ten pounds.”
passages.vernacular: 「長鰭金槍魚,」佢大聲講。「牠會係好好嘅餌。牠有十磅重。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「長鰭金槍魚,」他大聲說。「牠會是很好的餌。牠有十磅重。」

passages.original: He did not remember when he had first started to talk aloud when he was by himself. He had sung when he was by himself in the old days and he had sung at night sometimes when he was alone steering on his watch in the smacks or in the turtle boats. He had probably started to talk aloud, when alone, when the boy had left. But he did not remember. When he and the boy fished together they usually spoke only when it was necessary. They talked at night or when they were storm-bound by bad weather. It was considered a virtue not to talk unnecessarily at sea and the old man had always considered it so and respected it. But now he said his thoughts aloud many times since there was no one that they could annoy.
passages.vernacular: 佢不記得自己從乜嘢時候起,一個人時開始大聲講話。過去佢一個人時唱歌,有時夜裡獨自在漁船或海龜船上值班掌舵時都唱。佢大概係從男孩離開時,開始獨自大聲講話嘅。但佢不記得喇。佢同男孩一起捕魚時,通常只喺必要時才講話。佢哋夜裡講話,或者被壞天氣困住時講話。喺海上唔使要地講話被認為係不好嘅,老人一向咁樣認為,並尊重佢。但而家佢多次把佢嘅想法講出聲,因為冇人會被打擾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不記得自己從什麼時候起,一個人時開始大聲說話。過去他一個人時唱歌,有時夜裡獨自在漁船或海龜船上值班掌舵時也唱。他大概是從男孩離開時,開始獨自大聲說話的。但他不記得了。他和男孩一起捕魚時,通常只在必要時才說話。他們夜裡說話,或者被壞天氣困住時說話。在海上不必要地說話被認為是不好的,老人一向這樣認為,並尊重它。但現在他多次把他的想法說出聲,因為沒有人會被打擾。

passages.original: “If the others heard me talking out loud they would think that I am crazy,” he said aloud. “But since I am not crazy, I do not care. And the rich have radios to talk to them in their boats and to bring them the baseball.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果別人聽到我大聲講話,佢哋會認為我瘋喇,」佢大聲講。「但既然我冇瘋,我不在乎。而且有錢人喺佢哋嘅船上有收音機同佢哋講話,畀佢哋帶嚟棒球。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果別人聽到我大聲說話,他們會認為我瘋了,」他大聲說。「但既然我沒瘋,我不在乎。而且有錢人在他們的船上有收音機同他們說話,給他們帶來棒球。」

passages.original: Now is no time to think of baseball, he thought. Now is the time to think of only one thing. That which I was born for. There might be a big one around that school, he thought. I picked up only a straggler from the albacore that were feeding. But they are working far out and fast. Everything that shows on the surface today travels very fast and to the north-east. Can that be the time of day? Or is it some sign of weather that I do not know?
passages.vernacular: 而家唔係想棒球嘅時候,佢想。而家係只想一件事嘅時候。我生來要做嘅嗰件事。嗰群魚周圍可能有一條大嘅,佢想。我只撿到咗喺進食嘅長鰭金槍魚嘅一條落伍者。但牠哋喺遠處快速活動。今日水面上出現嘅一切嘢都走得好快,往東北方向。嗰會係一天中嘅時間嗎?定係某種我唔知道嘅天氣徵兆?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在不是想棒球的時候,他想。現在是只想一件事的時候。我生來要做的那件事。那群魚周圍可能有一條大的,他想。我只撿到了在進食的長鰭金槍魚的一條落伍者。但牠們在遠處快速活動。今天水面上出現的一切東西都走得很快,往東北方向。那會是一天中的時間嗎?還是某種我不知道的天氣徵兆?

passages.original: He could not see the green of the shore now but only the tops of the blue hills that showed white as though they were snow-capped and the clouds that looked like high snow mountains above them. The sea was very dark and the light made prisms in the water. The myriad flecks of the plankton were annulled now by the high sun and it was only the great deep prisms in the blue water that the old man saw now with his lines going straight down into the water that was a mile deep.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家睇唔見岸上嘅綠色,只睇到藍色山丘嘅頂部,佢哋顯得雪白,好像戴住雪帽,同佢哋上面睇起嚟像高大雪山嘅雲。海好暗,光喺水中形成稜鏡。無數嘅浮游生物斑點而家被高高嘅太陽抵消喇,老人而家只睇到藍水中巨大嘅深色稜鏡,佢嘅線直直沉入一英里深嘅水中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他現在看不見岸上的綠色,只看到藍色山丘的頂部,它們顯得雪白,好像戴著雪帽,和它們上面看起來像高大雪山的雲。海很暗,光在水中形成稜鏡。無數的浮游生物斑點現在被高高的太陽抵消了,老人現在只看到藍水中巨大的深色稜鏡,他的線直直沉入一英里深的水中。

passages.original: The tuna, the fishermen called all the fish of that species tuna and only distinguished among them by their proper names when they came to sell them or to trade them for baits, were down again. The sun was hot now and the old man felt it on the back of his neck and felt the sweat trickle down his back as he rowed.
passages.vernacular: 金槍魚,漁夫哋把呢個種類嘅所有魚都叫金槍魚,只喺賣掉或換餌時才用牠哋各自嘅名字區分,又下去喇。太陽而家好熱,老人喺後頸上感覺到佢,感覺汗水順住背流下,佢划住船。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 金槍魚,漁夫們把這個種類的所有魚都叫金槍魚,只在賣掉或換餌時才用牠們各自的名字區分,又下去了。太陽現在很熱,老人在後頸上感覺到它,感覺汗水順著背流下,他划著船。

passages.original: I could just drift, he thought, and sleep and put a bight of line around my toe to wake me. But today is eighty-five days and I should fish the day well.
passages.vernacular: 我可以隨波漂流,佢想,瞓覺,喺腳趾上繞一圈線把我弄醒。但今日係第八十五天,我應該好好捕魚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以隨波漂流,他想,睡覺,在腳趾上繞一圈線把我弄醒。但今天是第八十五天,我應該好好捕魚。

chapters.title: III. The Great Fish 大魚上鉤

passages.original: Just then, watching his lines, he saw one of the projecting green sticks dip sharply.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢陣,佢睇住佢嘅線,睇到一根伸出去嘅綠樹枝猛地下沉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這時,他看著他的線,看到一根伸出去的綠樹枝猛地下沉。

passages.original: “Yes,” he said. “Yes,” and shipped his oars without bumping the boat. He reached out for the line and held it softly between the thumb and forefinger of his right hand. He felt no strain nor weight and he held the line lightly. Then it came again. This time it was a tentative pull, not solid nor heavy, and he knew exactly what it was. One hundred fathoms down a marlin was eating the sardines that covered the point and the shank of the hook where the hand-forged hook projected from the head of the small tuna.
passages.vernacular: 「係喇,」佢講。「係喇,」並收起槳,冇碰到船。佢伸手去握住線,用右手拇指同食指輕輕捏住。佢冇感到拉力,都冇重量,佢輕輕握住線。然後佢又嚟喇。呢一次係試探性嘅一拉,不結實,都不重,佢確切地知道嗰個係乜嘢。喺一百噚深處,一條馬林魚正在食沙丁魚,嗰啲沙丁魚蓋住咗從小金槍魚頭部伸出嚟嘅手工鍛造嘅魚鉤嘅尖端同柄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是了,」他說。「是了,」並收起槳,沒有碰到船。他伸手去握住線,用右手拇指和食指輕輕捏著。他沒有感到拉力,也沒有重量,他輕輕握著線。然後它又來了。這一次是試探性的一拉,不結實,也不重,他確切地知道那是什麼。在一百噚深處,一條馬林魚正在吃沙丁魚,那些沙丁魚蓋住了從小金槍魚頭部伸出來的手工鍛造的魚鉤的尖端和柄。

passages.original: The old man held the line delicately, and softly, with his left hand, unleashed it from the stick. Now he could let it run through his fingers without the fish feeling any tension.
passages.vernacular: 老人精細而輕柔地握住線,用左手把佢從樹枝上解開。而家佢可以讓佢從指間滑過,而魚感覺唔到任何張力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老人精細而輕柔地握著線,用左手把它從樹枝上解開。現在他可以讓它從指間滑過,而魚感覺不到任何張力。

passages.original: This far out, he must be huge in this month, he thought. Eat them, fish. Eat them. Please eat them. How fresh they are and you down there six hundred feet in that cold water in the dark. Make another turn in the dark and come back and eat them.
passages.vernacular: 咁遠嘅地方,呢個月份,佢一定好大,佢想。食吧,魚。食牠哋。請食牠哋。牠哋幾咁新鮮,而你喺下面六百英尺嘅冷水裡,喺黑暗中。喺黑暗中再轉個圈,回嚟食牠哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這麼遠的地方,這個月份,他一定很大,他想。吃吧,魚。吃牠們。請吃牠們。牠們多麼新鮮,而你在下面六百英尺的冷水裡,在黑暗中。在黑暗中再轉個圈,回來吃牠們。

passages.original: He felt the light delicate pulling and then a harder pull when a sardine’s head must have been more difficult to break from the hook. Then there was nothing.
passages.vernacular: 佢感到輕輕嘅、細微嘅拉扯,然後係更用力嘅一拉,可能係一條沙丁魚嘅頭更難從鉤上扯下嚟。然後乜嘢都冇喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他感到輕輕的、細微的拉扯,然後是更用力的一拉,可能是一條沙丁魚的頭更難從鉤上扯下來。然後什麼也沒有了。

passages.original: “Come on,” the old man said aloud. “Make another turn. Just smell them. Aren’t they lovely? Eat them good now and then there is the tuna. Hard and cold and lovely. Don’t be shy, fish. Eat them.”
passages.vernacular: 「嚟啊,」老人大聲講。「再轉一圈。只要聞聞牠哋。牠哋不可愛嗎?好好食牠哋,然後仲有金槍魚。結實、冰冷、可愛。別害羞,魚。食吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「來啊,」老人大聲說。「再轉一圈。只要聞聞牠們。牠們不可愛嗎?好好吃牠們,然後還有金槍魚。結實、冰冷、可愛。別害羞,魚。吃吧。」

passages.original: He waited with the line between his thumb and his finger, watching it and the other lines at the same time for the fish might have swum up or down. Then came the same delicate pulling touch again.
passages.vernacular: 佢拇指同食指夾住線等待,同時盯住佢同其他線,因為魚可能向上或向下游。然後同樣細微嘅拉扯又嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他拇指和食指夾著線等待,同時盯著它和其他線,因為魚可能向上或向下游。然後同樣細微的拉扯又來了。

passages.original: “He’ll take it,” the old man said aloud. “God help him to take it.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢會食嘅,」老人大聲講。「上帝保佑佢食。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他會吃的,」老人大聲說。「上帝保佑他吃。」

passages.original: He did not take it though. He was gone and the old man felt nothing.
passages.vernacular: 但佢冇食。佢走喇,老人乜嘢都冇感覺到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他沒有吃。他走了,老人什麼也沒感覺到。

passages.original: “He can’t have gone,” he said. “Christ knows he can’t have gone. He’s making a turn. Maybe he has been hooked before and he remembers something of it.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢唔可能走喇,」佢講。「基督知道佢唔可能走喇。佢喺轉圈。或者佢以前被鉤過,記得啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他不可能走了,」他說。「基督知道他不可能走了。他在轉圈。也許他以前被鉤過,記得一點。」

passages.original: Then he felt the gentle touch on the line and he was happy.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢感覺到線上輕輕嘅觸碰,佢好高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他感覺到線上輕輕的觸碰,他很高興。

passages.original: “It was only his turn,” he said. “He’ll take it.”
passages.vernacular: 「只係佢喺轉圈,」佢講。「佢會食嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只是他在轉圈,」他說。「他會吃的。」

passages.original: He was happy feeling the gentle pulling and then he felt something hard and unbelievably heavy. It was the weight of the fish and he let the line slip down, down, down, unrolling off the first of the two reserve coils. As it went down, slipping lightly through the old man’s fingers, he still could feel the great weight, though the pressure of his thumb and finger were almost imperceptible.
passages.vernacular: 佢高興地感覺住輕輕嘅拉扯,然後感覺到某種堅硬、重得難以置信嘅嘢。嗰個係魚嘅重量,佢讓線往下滑,往下,往下,從兩個備用線圈嘅第一個上展開。線往下滑,輕輕地從老人嘅指間滑過時,佢仍能感覺到巨大嘅重量,雖然佢拇指同食指嘅壓力幾乎感覺唔到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他高興地感覺著輕輕的拉扯,然後感覺到某種堅硬、重得難以置信的東西。那是魚的重量,他讓線往下滑,往下,往下,從兩個備用線圈的第一個上展開。線往下滑,輕輕地從老人的指間滑過時,他仍能感覺到巨大的重量,雖然他拇指和食指的壓力幾乎感覺不到。

passages.original: “What a fish,” he said. “He has it sideways in his mouth now and he is moving off with it.”
passages.vernacular: 「好大嘅魚,」佢講。「佢而家把佢橫住含喺嘴裡,正帶住佢游走。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好大的魚,」他說。「他現在把它橫著含在嘴裡,正帶著它游走。」

passages.original: Then he will turn and swallow it, he thought. He did not say that because he knew that if you said a good thing it might not happen. He knew what a huge fish this was and he thought of him moving away in the darkness with the tuna held crosswise in his mouth. At that moment he felt him stop moving but the weight was still there. Then the weight increased and he gave more line. He tightened the pressure of his thumb and finger for a moment and the weight increased and was going straight down.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢會轉身把佢吞下去,佢想。佢冇講出嚟,因為佢知道,如果你講出好事,佢可能就不發生喇。佢知道呢個係多大嘅一條魚,佢想像佢喺黑暗中游走,嘴裡橫含住金槍魚。呢陣佢感覺到牠停止咗移動,但重量仍喺嗰度。然後重量增加喇,佢放出更多線。佢暫時收緊拇指同食指嘅壓力,重量增加喇,並且直直往下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他會轉身把它吞下去,他想。他沒有說出來,因為他知道,如果你說出好事,它可能就不發生了。他知道這是多大的一條魚,他想像他在黑暗中游走,嘴裡橫含著金槍魚。這時他感覺到牠停止了移動,但重量仍在那裡。然後重量增加了,他放出更多線。他暫時收緊拇指和食指的壓力,重量增加了,並且直直往下去。

passages.original: “He’s taken it,” he said. “Now I’ll let him eat it well.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢食喇,」佢講。「而家我讓佢好好食。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他吃了,」他說。「現在我讓他好好吃。」

passages.original: He let the line slip through his fingers while he reached down with his left hand and made fast the free end of the two reserve coils to the loop of the two reserve coils of the next line. Now he was ready. He had three forty-fathom coils of line in reserve now, as well as the coil he was using.
passages.vernacular: 佢讓線從指間滑過,同時用左手伸下去,把兩個備用線圈嘅自由端繫牢喺下一根線嘅兩個備用線圈嘅環上。而家佢準備好喇。佢而家有三個四十噚嘅線圈作備用,加上佢正在使用嘅線圈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他讓線從指間滑過,同時用左手伸下去,把兩個備用線圈的自由端繫牢在下一根線的兩個備用線圈的環上。現在他準備好了。他現在有三個四十噚的線圈作備用,加上他正在使用的線圈。

passages.original: “Eat it a little more,” he said. “Eat it well.”
passages.vernacular: 「再多食啲,」佢講。「好好食。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再多吃一點,」他說。「好好吃。」

passages.original: Eat it so that the point of the hook goes into your heart and kills you, he thought. Come up easy and let me put the harpoon into you. All right. Are you ready? Have you been long enough at table?
passages.vernacular: 食吧,讓魚鉤嘅尖端扎進你嘅心,殺死你,佢想。輕輕上嚟,讓我把魚叉扎進你身上。好喇。你準備好咗嗎?你喺桌邊坐夠久咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吃吧,讓魚鉤的尖端扎進你的心,殺死你,他想。輕輕上來,讓我把魚叉扎進你身上。好了。你準備好了嗎?你在桌邊坐夠久了嗎?

passages.original: “Now!” he said aloud and struck hard with both hands, gained a yard of line and then struck again and again, swinging with each arm alternately on the cord with all the strength of his arms and the pivoted weight of his body.
passages.vernacular: 「而家!」佢大聲講,用雙手猛拉,得到一碼線,然後一次又一次猛拉,兩條手臂交替地擺動,用上手臂全部嘅力量同身體旋轉嘅重量。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在!」他大聲說,用雙手猛拉,得到一碼線,然後一次又一次猛拉,兩條手臂交替地擺動,用上手臂全部的力量和身體旋轉的重量。

passages.original: Nothing happened. The fish just moved away slowly and the old man could not raise him an inch. His line was strong and made for heavy fish and he held it against his back until it was so taut that beads of water were jumping from it. Then it began to make a slow hissing sound in the water and he still held it, bracing himself against the thwart and leaning back against the pull. The boat began to move slowly off toward the North-West.
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢都冇發生。魚只係慢慢游開,老人一寸都拉不動牠。佢嘅線好結實,係為重魚做嘅,佢把佢頂喺背上,直到佢繃得咁緊,水珠從上面跳出嚟。然後佢開始喺水中發出緩慢嘅嘶嘶聲,佢仍握住佢,身體頂住橫板,向後靠住拉力。小艇開始慢慢向西北移動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼也沒有發生。魚只是慢慢游開,老人一寸也拉不動牠。他的線很結實,是為重魚做的,他把它頂在背上,直到它繃得那麼緊,水珠從上面跳出來。然後它開始在水中發出緩慢的嘶嘶聲,他仍握著它,身體頂住橫板,向後靠著拉力。小艇開始慢慢向西北移動。

passages.original: The fish moved steadily and they travelled slowly on the calm water. The other baits were still in the water but there was nothing to be done.
passages.vernacular: 魚穩定地移動,佢哋喺平靜嘅水面上緩緩行進。其他嘅餌仍喺水中,但冇辦法可想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 魚穩定地移動,它們在平靜的水面上緩緩行進。其他的餌仍在水中,但沒有辦法可想。

passages.original: “I wish I had the boy,” the old man said aloud. “I’m being towed by a fish and I’m the towing bitt. I could make the line fast. But then he could break it. I must hold him all I can and give him line when he must have it. Thank God he is travelling and not going down.”
passages.vernacular: 「我真希望有嗰個男孩,」老人大聲講。「我被一條魚拖住,而我係纜柱。我可以把線繫牢。但嗰樣佢可能把佢扯斷。我必須盡我所能握住佢,必須時畀佢放線。謝天謝地佢係喺前進,而唔係往下。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真希望有那個男孩,」老人大聲說。「我被一條魚拖著,而我是纜柱。我可以把線繫牢。但那樣他可能把它扯斷。我必須盡我所能握住他,必須時給他放線。謝天謝地他是在前進,而不是往下。」

passages.original: What I will do if he decides to go down, I don’t know. What I’ll do if he sounds and dies I don’t know. But I’ll do something. There are plenty of things I can do.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢決定往下潛,我點算,我唔知道。如果佢下沉死去,我點算,我唔知道。但我會做點乜嘢。我能做嘅事情好多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他決定往下潛,我怎麼辦,我不知道。如果他下沉死去,我怎麼辦,我不知道。但我會做點什麼。我能做的事情很多。

passages.original: He held the line against his back and watched its slant in the water and the skiff moving steadily to the North-West.
passages.vernacular: 佢把線頂喺背上,睇住佢喺水中嘅斜度,同小艇穩定地向西北移動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把線頂在背上,看著它在水中的斜度,和小艇穩定地向西北移動。

passages.original: This will kill him, the old man thought. He can’t do this forever. But four hours later the fish was still swimming steadily out to sea, towing the skiff, and the old man was still braced solidly with the line across his back.
passages.vernacular: 呢會殺死佢,老人想。佢唔可能永遠咁樣。但四小時後,魚仍喺穩定地向海上游去,拖住小艇,老人仍牢固地撐住,線橫過佢嘅背。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這會殺死他,老人想。他不可能永遠這樣。但四小時後,魚仍在穩定地向海上游去,拖著小艇,老人仍牢固地撐著,線橫過他的背。

passages.original: “It was noon when I hooked him,” he said. “And I have never seen him.”
passages.vernacular: 「我鉤住佢時係正午,」佢講。「而我仲從冇見過佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我鉤住他時是正午,」他說。「而我還從沒見過他。」

passages.original: He had pushed his straw hat hard down on his head before he hooked the fish and it was cutting his forehead.
