passages.original: Finally he put the mast down and stood up. He picked the mast up and put it on his shoulder and started up the road. He had to sit down five times before he reached his shack.
passages.vernacular: 最後佢放下桅杆,站起嚟。佢把桅杆攞起嚟扛喺肩上,開始沿路走。佢到達小屋前唔得不坐下休息五次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後他放下桅杆,站起來。他把桅杆拿起來扛在肩上,開始沿路走。他到達小屋前不得不坐下休息五次。

passages.original: Inside the shack he leaned the mast against the wall. In the dark he found a water bottle and took a drink. Then he lay down on the bed. He pulled the blanket over his shoulders and then over his back and legs and he slept face down on the newspapers with his arms out straight and the palms of his hands up.
passages.vernacular: 喺小屋裡,佢把桅杆靠喺牆上。喺黑暗中佢找到一個水瓶,飲咗一口。然後佢躺到床上。佢把毯子拉過肩膀,然後過背同腿,臉朝下瞓喺報紙上,雙臂伸直,手掌向上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在小屋裡,他把桅杆靠在牆上。在黑暗中他找到一個水瓶,喝了一口。然後他躺到床上。他把毯子拉過肩膀,然後過背和腿,臉朝下睡在報紙上,雙臂伸直,手掌向上。

chapters.title: IX. The Boy Returns 男孩回來了

passages.original: He was asleep when the boy looked in the door in the morning. It was blowing so hard that the drifting-boats would not be going out and the boy had slept late and then come to the old man’s shack as he had come each morning. The boy saw that the old man was breathing and then he saw the old man’s hands and he started to cry. He went out very quietly to go to bring some coffee and all the way down the road he was crying.
passages.vernacular: 早晨男孩往門裡睇時,佢仲喺瞓。風颳得咁猛,漂網船都唔會出海,男孩瞓得晚,然後像每天早晨一樣嚟到老人嘅小屋。男孩睇到老人喺呼吸,然後睇到老人嘅手,佢開始哭喇。佢好輕地走出去,去攞些咖啡,一路上佢都喺哭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早晨男孩往門裡看時,他還在睡。風颳得那麼猛,漂網船都不會出海,男孩睡得晚,然後像每天早晨一樣來到老人的小屋。男孩看到老人在呼吸,然後看到老人的手,他開始哭了。他非常輕地走出去,去拿些咖啡,一路上他都在哭。

passages.original: Many fishermen were around the skiff looking at what was lashed beside it and one was in the water, his trousers rolled up, measuring the skeleton with a length of line.
passages.vernacular: 許多漁夫圍喺小艇旁邊,睇綁喺旁邊嘅嘢,其中一個站喺水裡,褲腿捲起,用一段線量嗰具骨架。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 許多漁夫圍在小艇旁邊,看綁在旁邊的東西,其中一個站在水裡,褲腿捲起,用一段線量那具骨架。

passages.original: The boy did not go down. He had been there before and one of the fishermen was looking after the skiff for him.
passages.vernacular: 男孩冇下去。佢以前去過嗰度,有個漁夫喺替佢睇住小艇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩沒有下去。他以前去過那裡,有個漁夫在替他看著小艇。

passages.original: “How is he?” one of the fishermen shouted.
passages.vernacular: 「佢點樣?」一個漁夫喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他怎麼樣?」一個漁夫喊道。

passages.original: “Sleeping,” the boy called. He did not care that they saw him crying. “Let no one disturb him.”
passages.vernacular: 「喺瞓覺,」男孩喊回去。佢不在乎佢哋睇見佢哭。「唔好畀任何人打擾佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在睡覺,」男孩喊回去。他不在乎他們看見他哭。「別讓任何人打擾他。」

passages.original: “He was eighteen feet from nose to tail,” the fisherman who was measuring him called.
passages.vernacular: 「佢從鼻子到尾巴有十八英尺,」正在量嘅漁夫喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他從鼻子到尾巴有十八英尺,」正在量的漁夫喊道。

passages.original: “I believe it,” the boy said.
passages.vernacular: 「我相信,」男孩講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我相信,」男孩說。

passages.original: He went into the Terrace and asked for a can of coffee.
passages.vernacular: 佢走進露台餐館,要咗一罐咖啡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他走進露台餐館,要了一罐咖啡。

passages.original: “Hot and with plenty of milk and sugar in it.”
passages.vernacular: 「要熱嘅,加好多奶同糖。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「要熱的,加很多奶和糖。」

passages.original: “Anything more?”
passages.vernacular: 「仲要乜嘢嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還要什麼嗎?」

passages.original: “No. Afterwards I will see what he can eat.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔好。之後我再睇佢能食乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不要。之後我再看他能吃什麼。」

passages.original: “What a fish it was,” the proprietor said. “There has never been such a fish. Those were two fine fish you took yesterday too.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係點樣嘅一條魚啊,」店主講。「從來冇過嗰樣嘅魚。你尋日抓嘅嗰兩條都係好魚。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是怎樣的一條魚啊,」店主說。「從來沒有過那樣的魚。你昨天抓的那兩條也是好魚。」

passages.original: “Damn my fish,” the boy said and he started to cry again.
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅魚去佢嘅,」男孩講,又開始哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的魚去他的,」男孩說,又開始哭了。

passages.original: “Do you want a drink of any kind?” the proprietor asked.
passages.vernacular: 「你要飲點乜嘢嗎?」店主問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你要喝點什麼嗎?」店主問。

passages.original: “No,” the boy said. “Tell them not to bother Santiago. I’ll be back.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔好,」男孩講。「告訴佢哋唔好打擾聖地亞哥。我會回嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不要,」男孩說。「告訴他們不要打擾聖地亞哥。我會回來。」

passages.original: “Tell him how sorry I am.”
passages.vernacular: 「告訴佢我幾咁難過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「告訴他我多麼難過。」

passages.original: “Thanks,” the boy said.
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝,」男孩講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝,」男孩說。

passages.original: The boy carried the hot can of coffee up to the old man’s shack and sat by him until he woke. Once it looked as though he were waking. But he had gone back into heavy sleep and the boy had gone across the road to borrow some wood to heat the coffee.
passages.vernacular: 男孩把熱咖啡罐攞到老人嘅小屋,坐喺佢旁邊,直到佢醒嚟。有一次睇起嚟佢快醒喇。但佢又回到咗沉瞓中,男孩過到路對面去借些木頭嚟熱咖啡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩把熱咖啡罐拿到老人的小屋,坐在他旁邊,直到他醒來。有一次看起來他快醒了。但他又回到了沉睡中,男孩過到路對面去借些木頭來熱咖啡。

passages.original: Finally the old man woke.
passages.vernacular: 終於老人醒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 終於老人醒了。

passages.original: “Don’t sit up,” the boy said. “Drink this.” He poured some of the coffee in a glass.
passages.vernacular: 「別坐起嚟,」男孩講。「飲呢個。」佢把啲咖啡倒進玻璃杯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別坐起來,」男孩說。「喝這個。」他把一些咖啡倒進玻璃杯。

passages.original: The old man took it and drank it.
passages.vernacular: 老人接過嚟飲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老人接過來喝了。

passages.original: “They beat me, Manolin,” he said. “They truly beat me.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋打敗咗我,馬諾林,」佢講。「佢哋真嘅打敗咗我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們打敗了我,馬諾林,」他說。「他們真的打敗了我。」

passages.original: “He didn’t beat you. Not the fish.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢冇打敗你。唔係嗰條魚。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他沒有打敗你。不是那條魚。」

passages.original: “No. Truly. It was afterwards.”
passages.vernacular: 「不。真嘅。係後來嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不。真的。是後來的事。」

passages.original: “Pedrico is looking after the skiff and the gear. What do you want done with the head?”
passages.vernacular: 「佩德里科喺睇管小艇同裝備。你想點處理魚頭?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「佩德里科在看管小艇和裝備。你想怎麼處理魚頭?」

passages.original: “Let Pedrico chop it up to use in fish traps.”
passages.vernacular: 「讓佩德里科把佢砍碎做魚籠。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓佩德里科把它砍碎做魚籠。」

passages.original: “And the spear?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰矛呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那矛呢?」

passages.original: “You keep it if you want it.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你要,你留住。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你要,你留著。」

passages.original: “I want it,” the boy said. “Now we must make our plans about the other things.”
passages.vernacular: 「我要,」男孩講。「而家我哋必須計畫其他嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要,」男孩說。「現在我們必須計畫其他的事。」

passages.original: “Did they search for me?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋找過我嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們找過我嗎?」

passages.original: “Of course. With coast guard and with planes.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然。有海岸警衛隊同飛機。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然。有海岸警衛隊和飛機。」

passages.original: “The ocean is very big and a skiff is small and hard to see,” the old man said. He noticed how pleasant it was to have someone to talk to instead of speaking only to himself and to the sea. “I missed you,” he said. “What did you catch?”
passages.vernacular: 「海洋好大,小艇好小,好難睇見,」老人講。佢注意到有人可以講話係幾咁愉快,而唔係只對自己同對海講話。「我想念你,」佢講。「你捕到咗乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「海洋很大,小艇很小,很難看見,」老人說。他注意到有人可以說話是多麼愉快,而不是只對自己和對海說話。「我想念你,」他說。「你捕到了什麼?」

passages.original: “One the first day. One the second and two the third.”
passages.vernacular: 「第一天一條。第二天一條,第三天兩條。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「第一天一條。第二天一條,第三天兩條。」

passages.original: “Very good.”
passages.vernacular: 「好好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好。」

passages.original: “Now we fish together again.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家我哋又一起捕魚喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在我們又一起捕魚了。」

passages.original: “No. I am not lucky. I am not lucky anymore.”
passages.vernacular: 「不。我冇運氣。我唔再有運氣喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不。我沒有運氣。我不再有運氣了。」

passages.original: “The hell with luck,” the boy said. “I’ll bring the luck with me.”
passages.vernacular: 「去佢嘅運氣,」男孩講。「我把運氣帶嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「去他的運氣,」男孩說。「我把運氣帶來。」

passages.original: “What will your family say?”
passages.vernacular: 「你家人會點講?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你家人會怎麼說?」

passages.original: “I do not care. I caught two yesterday. But we will fish together now for I still have much to learn.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不在乎。我尋日抓咗兩條。但我哋而家要一起捕魚,因為我仲有好多要學。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不在乎。我昨天抓了兩條。但我們現在要一起捕魚,因為我還有很多要學。」

passages.original: “We must get a good killing lance and always have it on board. You can make the blade from a spring leaf from an old Ford. We can grind it in Guanabacoa. It should be sharp and not tempered so it will break. My knife broke.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋必須弄一支好嘅殺魚長矛,總是帶喺船上。你可以用舊福特車嘅一片彈簧鋼做刀刃。我哋可以到瓜納巴科阿去磨。佢應該鋒利,唔好回火,以免折斷。我嘅刀折斷喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們必須弄一支好的殺魚長矛,總是帶在船上。你可以用舊福特車的一片彈簧鋼做刀刃。我們可以到瓜納巴科阿去磨。它應該鋒利,不要回火,以免折斷。我的刀折斷了。」

passages.original: “I’ll get another knife and have the spring ground. How many days of heavy brisa have we?”
passages.vernacular: 「我再弄一把刀,把彈簧磨好。強風仲有幾天?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我再弄一把刀,把彈簧磨好。強風還有幾天?」

passages.original: “Maybe three. Maybe more.”
passages.vernacular: 「或者三天。或者更多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許三天。也許更多。」

passages.original: “I will have everything in order,” the boy said. “You get your hands well old man.”
passages.vernacular: 「我會把一切整理好,」男孩講。「你把手養好,老人家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會把一切整理好,」男孩說。「你把手養好,老人家。」

passages.original: “I know how to care for them. In the night I spat something strange and felt something in my chest was broken.”
passages.vernacular: 「我知道點照顧佢哋。夜裡我吐咗啲奇怪嘅嘢,覺得胸口有乜嘢斷喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道怎麼照顧它們。夜裡我吐了一些奇怪的東西,覺得胸口有什麼斷了。」

passages.original: “Get that well too,” the boy said. “Lie down, old man, and I will bring you your clean shirt. And something to eat.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰都要養好,」男孩講。「躺下,老人家,我畀你攞乾淨襯衫嚟。仲有食嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那也要養好,」男孩說。「躺下,老人家,我給你拿乾淨襯衫來。還有吃的。」

passages.original: “Bring any of the papers of the time that I was gone,” the old man said.
passages.vernacular: 「把我不喺嗰段時間嘅報紙帶嚟,」老人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「把我不在那段時間的報紙帶來,」老人說。

passages.original: “You must get well fast for there is much that I can learn and you can teach me everything. How much did you suffer?”
passages.vernacular: 「你必須快點好起嚟,因為我有好多可以學,你能教我所有嘅嘢。你受咗多少苦?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你必須快點好起來,因為我有很多可以學,你能教我所有的東西。你受了多少苦?」

passages.original: “Plenty,” the old man said.
passages.vernacular: 「好多,」老人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很多,」老人說。

passages.original: “I’ll bring the food and the papers,” the boy said. “Rest well, old man. I will bring stuff from the drug-store for your hands.”
passages.vernacular: 「我帶食物同報紙嚟,」男孩講。「好好休息,老人家。我從藥店畀你嘅手攞些藥嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我帶食物和報紙來,」男孩說。「好好休息,老人家。我從藥店給你的手拿些藥來。」

passages.original: “Don’t forget to tell Pedrico the head is his.”
passages.vernacular: 「別忘咗告訴佩德里科,魚頭係佢嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別忘了告訴佩德里科,魚頭是他的。」

passages.original: “No. I will remember.”
passages.vernacular: 「不。我會記住。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不。我會記住。」

passages.original: As the boy went out the door and down the worn coral rock road he was crying again.
passages.vernacular: 男孩走出門,走喺磨損嘅珊瑚石路上時,又哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩走出門,走在磨損的珊瑚石路上時,又哭了。

passages.original: That afternoon there was a party of tourists at the Terrace and looking down in the water among the empty beer cans and dead barracudas a woman saw a great long white spine with a huge tail at the end that lifted and swung with the tide while the east wind blew a heavy steady sea outside the entrance to the harbour.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天下午,露台餐館有一批遊客,一個女人往下睇水裡,喺空啤酒罐同死梭子魚之間,睇到一條巨大長長嘅白色脊骨,末端有一條巨大嘅尾巴,隨住潮水升起搖擺,而東風喺港口入口外吹起沉重而穩定嘅海浪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天下午,露台餐館有一批遊客,一個女人往下看水裡,在空啤酒罐和死梭子魚之間,看到一條巨大長長的白色脊骨,末端有一條巨大的尾巴,隨著潮水升起搖擺,而東風在港口入口外吹起沉重而穩定的海浪。

passages.original: “What’s that?” she asked a waiter and pointed to the long backbone of the great fish that was now just garbage waiting to go out with the tide.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係乜嘢?」佢問一個服務員,指住嗰條大魚嘅長脊骨,佢而家不過係等住隨潮水漂走嘅垃圾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是什麼?」她問一個服務員,指著那條大魚的長脊骨,它現在不過是等著隨潮水漂走的垃圾。

passages.original: “Tiburon,” the waiter said, “Eshark.” He was meaning to explain what had happened.
passages.vernacular: 「鯊魚(Tiburón),」服務員講,「Eshark。」佢想解釋所發生嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「鯊魚(Tiburón),」服務員說,「Eshark。」他想解釋所發生的事。

passages.original: “I didn’t know sharks had such handsome, beautifully formed tails.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道鯊魚有咁好睇、形狀咁美嘅尾巴。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道鯊魚有這麼好看、形狀這麼美的尾巴。」

passages.original: “I didn’t either,” her male companion said.
passages.vernacular: 「我都唔知道,」佢嘅男伴講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也不知道,」她的男伴說。

passages.original: Up the road, in his shack, the old man was sleeping again. He was still sleeping on his face and the boy was sitting by him watching him. The old man was dreaming about the lions.
passages.vernacular: 沿路上去,喺佢嘅小屋裡,老人又瞓住喇。佢仍然臉朝下瞓,男孩坐喺佢旁邊睇住佢。老人正夢見獅子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沿路上去,在他的小屋裡,老人又睡著了。他仍然臉朝下睡,男孩坐在他旁邊看著他。老人正夢見獅子。
